title: Item sets and uniques
next:
BUILT. Same shape as BL-0081: the entry is a specification, every clause is in the tree, and the status never moved. Verified against the distinctive clauses rather than by counting files, because the two clauses that could plausibly have been skipped are the ones that matter.

  - game/src/modules/set_bonus/ with its own api.gd (ItemsApi still capped at 12), state in module_data set_state.
  - SETS KEYED BY SOURCE ID, never by a piece instance id, which is the clause the entry names explicitly and the one a piece-keyed implementation would fail. SetDef lists pieces and uniques as ids and answers membership from those ids, so the same set is stable across separately realized instances.
  - UNIQUES ARE AUTHORED IDENTITY, NOT RARITY. UniqueItem.TAG is a definition tag, is_unique reads it, and the comment is explicit that a unique is not "the only copy in the world". A unique carries a LOCKED SIGNATURE - the authored fixed options - and forge() preserves it untouched while topping up only the rolled channel, under a bounded limit so the top-up cannot grow without end.
  - UNIQUE DROP ROUTES are authored in res://data/sets/unique_routes.jsonl and read by unique_id, while the boss comes from the definition own unique_route:<boss_id> tag. The catalog comment states the rule this implements: identity comes from the definitions and never from the route index, so deleting or mistyping a route row cannot make a shipped unique disappear from a count or from a screen.
  - A unique counts toward a set threshold exactly like a piece (SetDef.members() sums both), and the route column cannot contradict set membership because membership is read from the definition.

title: Loot tables and boss/domain reward lifecycle
next:
BUILT. Third of the three WAVE-2 entries that were still todo for features already in the tree, verified clause by clause.

  - game/src/modules/loot/ with its own api.gd, state in module_data loot_state, ItemsApi untouched at 12 verbs.
  - CHANCE-ROLL AND WEIGHTED-CHOICE ARE SEMANTICALLY SEPARATE, which is the clause the entry names and the one worth checking because a single weighted pool with a 0..1 weight would look similar and be wrong. LootTableDef says "two counts live here and never mix": rolls..rolls_max is how many WEIGHTED DRAWS the table makes, each picking one candidate from the weighted pool, and weighted_entries() excludes anything that is not weighted, with the comment that those entries are "not part of the weighted competition" - that is the guaranteed and pure-chance channel kept out of the draw. rolls_max of 0 is how a pure chance or pure guaranteed table is authored, so the two semantics are authored as different tables rather than as a weight value.
  - ONE REWARD PAYLOAD PER ENCOUNTER with a persisted claim token is the behaviour game/tools/boot_probe.gd already proves in a real boot: a fight killed the boss, minted 2 rewards with 2 drops pending, and a pickup through the reward lists own control moved pending 2 to 1 and grew the bag 3 to 4 rows. The payload is minted once and the claim is the only way to move it.
  - 23 test files under game/tests/modules/loot.

Marked done on the artifact evidence above. NOT claimed: that all nine criteria pass - no suite was run this turn, the engine lock was held continuously. ItemsApi.use_item reaches inv.remove(def_id, quantity) only after ItemUse.apply returns ok, and apply returns the gate verbatim the moment spend_gate is non-empty (api.gd:167-171). spend_gate consults ProgressionRoles.role_of(def.id), which reads the AUTHORED table game/data/items/progression_roles.json - versioned at TABLE_VERSION 1 and REFUSED on a version mismatch rather than read as empty, precisely so a stale table cannot silently un-rule every pill and reopen this. That table carries 132 ruled ids, one row per item, keyed by item id and never by subtype because pill holds both progression pills and ordinary draughts.

The "activation channel that refuses inventory use and names the path it serves" this entry asks for is also built. The refusal is progression_input, it carries the role (body_breakthrough, mind_breakthrough, and so on), and tests/modules/items/test_progression_roles.gd cross-checks the table against the realm seeds in BOTH directions so a progression input cannot go unruled and a role cannot be invented for an item no seed names. Nothing is left to do here.

THE REAL RESIDUAL IS SMALLER AND IS A SECOND COPY OF THE GATE. ui/panels/item_action_rules.gd:33 use_block_reason is the UI mirror the file itself describes as mirroring the facade "for feedback". It knows not_usable and not_carried. It does NOT know progression_input - grep finds that string in three test files and in no file under game/src/ui/. So on a ruled pill the Use control is offered, the player presses it, and the screen reports the facade reason verbatim via _reject(String(result.get("reason"))) - the player sees the raw token "progression_input". Nothing is destroyed and the refusal is named, so this is not a safety hole; it is an affordance that lies about its own outcome.

The correct fix is NOT to grow ItemsApi: it is frozen at twelve verbs and AGENTS.md says a new need there means splitting the facade. generate is already the delivery verb a caller needs, and the mirror's own docstring concedes the facade is authoritative and a rejection is final. So the honest options are a facade split that publishes spend_gate, or the ui mirror reading the authored table itself - and the second is worse, because it is the second copy this file already is. Filed for the slice that owns items; not done here because game/src/modules/items belongs to whichever session claims it.

title: CLOSED AS STALE: zero authored drops are stranded, not 1500 - every table is reachable through the nested closure
next:
STALE. THE 1500 IS WRONG AND THE REAL NUMBER IS ZERO. Re-measured twice, independently, per BL-0619.

ROOT'S MEASUREMENT, derived from the .tres text alone with no code of anyone's in the loop. All 160 encounters parsed; 336 tables are bound by an authored tier band; walking the nested-table closure from those 336 reaches 1425 tables, which is every authored table in the corpus (game/data/loot/tables holds exactly 1425 .tres and HEAD holds the same count, so nothing authored is unaccounted for). Unpayable tables: 0. Items carried only on an unpayable table: 0. Items no defeat can pay at all: 0. The closure matters: a band binds 336 tables directly but those nest 1089 more, and measuring only the direct bindings is what produces a large scary number that does not exist.

WHAT CHANGED, and it is a content wave rather than a fix to this entry. Commit 31953e54 ("content(loot): host the sixth elemental guardian so its five items resolve") is the shape of the repair, and c0ab2689 is in the same neighbourhood. Entries like BL-0338 and BL-0681 closed the same class from the other end (orphan domains, an encounter with no domain_id). So the premise went stale underneath a tracked entry, which is precisely what BL-0619 warns about: nothing fails when a finding becomes untrue.

THE SUB-THRESHOLD RESIDUAL, which is the only part still worth carrying. Eight authored tables are bound by no band and nested by no table - dead weight rather than a soft-lock, because all 9 of their items are also carried as guaranteed=true entries on tables a defeat does pay (qi_qi_refining_guardian_core on loot_qi_qi_refining_guardian; body_nascent_soul_tempering_herb on the bound loot_route_e2_nascent_soul_herald). So no player is blocked and tools acquisition validate was green before and after. Whether to delete eight unreachable tables is an authoring call about dead content, NOT an OBTAINABLE defect, and it is deliberately not treated as one here.

WHY THIS ENTRY MATTERS AS A RECORD even though it is closed. It is the second time in two days that an item-program finding was asserted at scale and measured to nothing - the first was BL-0346's 483 unruled subtypes, now closed, where I found 0. Both numbers were large, both were specific, and neither was checked before work was scoped against it. The cost of a stale count is not the count; it is the rebuild of working code that follows from trusting it.

DO NOT trust a count in this file without re-deriving it. That is the whole lesson and it is why this entry is kept rather than deleted.

So a mind writer is a duplicate, and a gate is worse than a duplicate: nothing else on the mind path raises network resonance, so requiring it in strengthen_anchor would lock an actor who never trains body out of the R19+ anchor milestone entirely.
next: CLOSED 2026-10-04 by RE-MEASUREMENT (session mind-ledger). Both halves of this title are gone, and the second half is gone by DECISION not by omission. (1) The field is deleted: rg resonance_required over game/src, game/data and game/tests returns ZERO code hits - realm_seed.gd no longer declares it and none of the 30 .tres under game/data/mind_cultivation/realms/ author it. (2) 'Mind's resonance milestone never calls set_resonance_rank' is now answered 'and must not': docs/adr/0147-the-unread-mindrealmseed-fields-are-deleted-rather-than-wired.md:37-43 rules that MeridianNetwork.resonance_rank is ONE shared field written only by body_cultivation/training.gd, so a mind writer is a duplicate and a mind GATE is worse - nothing on the mind or qi path raises the rank, so requiring it in strengthen_anchor would lock any actor who never trains body out of the only verb that pays for the anchor. This entry's own next step prescribed exactly this deletion. RESIDUE, filed as a NEW id: the generator still emits the deleted line, so a regeneration re-authors it.

title: MISDIAGNOSED (the capacity penalty IS applied where the gate reads it): the real defect is that THREE definitions of full disagree and the two that disagree are the provider and the screen bar
source: The first half of this entry is wrong. effective_capacity() IS applied where the gate reads it: SeaOfConsciousness.ratio() uses it as its denominator at sea_of_consciousness.gd:44-46, and both advancement.gd:82 and breakthrough_condition.gd:31 gate on ratio(), so the turbulence penalty is live. The disagreement is real and is between three numbers: MindTraining.synchronize sets the pool maximum from structural_capacity at training.gd:31 and never from effective_capacity, so SeaOfConsciousness.is_full() (:51-52, no production caller - its eleven callers are all tests, including the fill wait in mind_gate_probe.gd:139), SeaProvider SEA_FULL (sea_provider.gd:17, compares against usable) and ratio() (usable) answer one question three ways, while the screen fill bar reads summary mind_power_max, which is the un-reduced pool maximum.
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL, and the disagreement is now exactly three numbers where it was three. (1) MindTraining.synchronize sets the pool maximum from structural_capacity at training.gd:37, never from effective_capacity. (2) SeaOfConsciousness.ratio() (sea_of_consciousness.gd:44-46) divides by effective_capacity, and BOTH the preview at advancement.gd:82 and the enforced gate at breakthrough_condition.gd:31 read ratio(), so the turbulence penalty IS live where the gate reads it - this entry's first half was right about that and stays dismissed. (3) The screen's fill bar reads summary().mind_power_max, which is sea.maximum(actor) (api.gd:126) - the un-reduced pool maximum. So the bar fills to 100% at a moment the gate still calls the sea not full, and the divergence is worst exactly when the sea is turbulent. Separately, SeaOfConsciousness.is_full() (sea_of_consciousness.gd:51) still has ZERO callers in game/src - every one of its callers is a test, including the fill wait in mind_gate_probe.gd:139 that the reachability audit depends on. Pick ONE definition of full and say which in ADR 0016. The cheapest correct move is to delete is_full and replace its test callers with a wait on ratio() >= sea_fill_required, because is_full is a second definition of a question ratio() already answers authoritatively. The alternative - set pool.set_maximum(effective_capacity) at training.gd:37 so the bar and the gate agree - is smaller but couples the bar to the turbulence penalty, which means the bar SHIFTS as turbulence changes and a player watching it sees the goalpost move. Either way, assert the chosen definition ONCE in test_sea_of_consciousness.gd; today three definitions and no assertion is what lets them drift. Do not delete is_full without replacing mind_gate_probe.fill_sea - the reachability audit loses its fill condition and BL-0129/BL-0311's lesson applies: never close a gate complaint by removing the gate's evidence.

title: UNDEFINED: sea catalyst changes nothing structural and nothing carries into the next realm
source: REAL and undefined, and it is the same defect BL-0157 sees from the other side. strengthen_sea at training.gd:157-175 consumes the catalyst and sets clarity, purity, and trained_stage = maxi(stored, 1); it never touches structural_capacity, sea_tier, or any stat, and synchronize rewrites tier and capacity from the NEXT realm seed on the next advance. The only thing that survives a realm change is trained_stage, which no gate reads.
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL and still undefined. strengthen_sea at training.gd:256-274 consumes the realm's sea_catalyst and then does exactly three things: sea.set_clarity(maxf(clarity, seed.clarity_required)), sea.set_purity(maxf(purity, seed.purity_required)), sea.trained_stage = maxi(trained_stage, 1), then synchronize(). It never touches structural_capacity, sea_tier, or any stat, and synchronize rewrites tier and capacity from the NEXT realm seed on the next advance. So nothing survives a realm change except trained_stage, which no gate reads (BL-0157). The DECISION, and it is an owner ruling: what does strengthening the sea buy beyond the two floors? Three coherent answers, pick one and write it down. (a) It buys nothing beyond the floors - then delete the verb, the catalyst field and the 30 authored catalyst items rather than ship a paid button whose only lasting effect is a number nothing reads. (b) It buys capacity - then write it into synchronize and gate the sea_fill term on it, which makes the paid verb move the gate that currently moves nothing. (c) It buys the trained_stage milestone - then give trained_stage a gate, which needs a per-realm authored field, and note that ADR 0147 DELETED the two work-budget fields that looked like that field (sea_milestone_work, meridian_milestone_work) on ADR 0096 grounds: a second mandatory cost on a boundary whose item is already mandatory, on the verb that raises the gate. So (c) is a reversal of ADR 0147 and needs its own ADR, not a wiring patch. DO NOT pay for this three times: BL-0140, BL-0145 and BL-0157 are ONE question. Settle it here (it is the design ruling), then BL-0157's field and BL-0140's row follow as consequences.
dispatch_note: the design ruling that governs BL-0140 and BL-0157; settle it first

title: BALANCE, NOT A DEFECT: the vacuity is fixed and guarded, but which gate SHOULD price the mind ladder is undecided - progress prices 21/29 boundaries and comprehension 8/29
source: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger). THE 'VACUOUS' CLAIM IS NOW FALSE, and it is false because BL-0165 moved the rate, not because anyone retuned a balance. The premise measured correctly for the shipped tree it was written against: with a flat INSIGHT_RATE of 0.05, test_mind_gate_binding.gd raced the two thresholds through MindTraining.cultivate at all 29 boundaries and comprehension priced 29/29 while progress priced 0/29 - state.progress was genuinely never the thing a player waited for. commit d21e2f64's predecessor BL-0165 then priced the insight rate off core Stat.INSIGHT_GAIN (training.gd:_grant_insight reads derived(INSIGHT_GAIN) BEFORE set_base, so a sitting is not priced at the rate its own gain implies), which bends the comprehension curve sub-linear and moves the split to progress 21/29 against comprehension 8/29. So progress now prices the majority of boundaries and neither gate is dead.
next: The vacuity is FIXED and the fix is guarded, so do not re-file the old claim: test_mind_gate_binding.gd:190 test_neither_cultivation_gate_is_vacuous asserts the INVARIANT (both gates price at least one boundary), with the recorded mutation INSIGHT_RATE 0.05 -> 0.5 giving 14816 passed / 4 failed and the message naming the measurement ('comprehension prices at least one boundary (measured: progress 29, comprehension 0)'). What is left is a BALANCE RULING and this entry now says so explicitly: should the progress bar or the comprehension floor be the thing a player waits for at most boundaries? The current answer is a 21/8 split with the deepest boundary inverted - R29->R30 needs roughly 30 sittings for comprehension against 64 for progress - which reads as the wrong way round for a path whose defining stat is comprehension (ADR 0013). Two coherent answers. (a) Comprehension should price the ladder: lower INSIGHT_RATE or raise CLARITY-free progress_required until comprehension dominates again, and accept a longer wait. (b) Progress should: accept that the mind path is a grind-and-cultivate path where the bar, not the floor, is the pacing signal. Either way the change is to authored numbers in the 30 seeds or one coefficient, NOT to a gate, and the invariant test must stay green after it. Recording the ruling in ADR 0013 or ADR 0024 is what stops the next agent re-measuring 21/29.

title: UNWIRED: filling the Sea of Consciousness changes no stat anything reads - MindProvider computes mind_power_ratio and discards it
source: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (BL-0619: the recorded source was stale and its central premise was FALSE). BL-0154 said filling the sea changes no stat anything reads because provider.gd discarded mind_power_ratio. Two things moved since. (1) The dead local is gone and guarded - provider.gd:29-40 now records why it was DELETED rather than wired, and test_mind_stat_surface.gd fails if mind_power_ratio/Stat.SPIRIT/comprehension_bonus return. (2) MORE IMPORTANT: MindDamage EXISTS and is bound. combat_engine/mind_damage.gd is a full ADR 0071 implementation registered at app/combat_boot.gd:61+143-151, and it reads SIX of the seven ids this module publishes. The old source claimed the ids only consumer was a MindDamage "which does not exist yet" - that was true when written and is not now. Full enumeration, every id MindProvider publishes and its production reader in res://src: mental_attack -> mind_damage.gd:228 (attacker side); mental_defense -> :230 (target side, the d/(d+base) mitigation input); illusion_resistance -> :575 (OBSCURE only, by design); mind_focus_chance -> :550 (spends FOCUS_MULT); mind_avoidance -> :563 (refunds COHERENCE_DAMP of coherence); mind_technique_power -> combat_damage.tres:39 mind_deviation_stat, read at mind_damage.gd:415-418 where apply_deviation zeroing it IS the collapse disarm; spiritual_sense_range -> NO reader that changes an outcome (ui/panels/stat_presenter.gd:134 only, which ADR 0124:44-46 defines as a readout). SeaProvider publishes one id, sea_capacity, also readout-only (stat_presenter.gd:144; BL-0142 owns it). Verified live, not by grep: test_mind_stat_reachability.gd asserts CombatBoot.bind_mechanisms binds MindDamage to a mind-only actor, asserts each resolved id is PUBLISHED under that exact spelling (a reader-side scan cannot see a publisher-side typo - that is how MUTATION-B passes an unchecked tree), and asserts the shipped tuning carries mind_stat_prefix="" so those bare ids really are the ones combat looks up. THE ANSWER IS (3) IT ALREADY READS, and the conclusion "no observable effect" is false twice over. Progression: the sea fill gates breakthrough at breakthrough_condition.gd:31 (sea.ratio >= sea_fill_required, authored 1.0 at all 30 seeds), already proven by test_mind_stat_surface.gd. Combat, newly proven here through the FACADE ONLY (no contribute() call): MindTraining.train_channel to STRENGTHENED raises MeridianNetwork.get_power_bonus, MindProvider multiplies it into mental_defense and mind_technique_power (ADR 0016:33 "Strengthening - increases mind technique power and mental defense"), MindDamage reads the first as its mitigation, so a mind strike erodes strictly less of the sea. test_mind_stat_reachability.gd::test_training_a_mind_channel_lowers_the_erosion_the_mechanism_resolves. Mutation proof, 60/0 baseline vs 51 passed/4 failed under MUTATION-A (meridian_power pinned to 0.0) and 56/4 under MUTATION-B (mental_defense published as "mind_defense"), both naming the behaviour; provider.gd restored byte-identical, sha256 23323BE2F57BE002164CF98BE3D78C364B4FFF5787241EBE3854946B88F54CAD, verified equal to pre-mutation commit f9d8ab5d. The one caveat that IS real is filed separately as BL-0651: the awareness pool has no writer anywhere in res://src, so both chance terms and coherence are constant. Not fixed here because the writer belongs to training.gd and WHAT funds awareness is an ADR question (ADR 0013:13 says refill, ADR 0071:35 says depleting spend).
next: CLOSE THIS ITEM on evidence - the reader exists, is registered, and six of seven ids are consumed. Do NOT re-add mind_power_ratio: ADR 0071 deliberately made the sea LEVEL the denominator (g /= defender_sea.structural_capacity) and named its defensive identity as four levers none of which is a fill-scaling stat, so a ratio-into-a-stat wiring is the lever that ADR ruled out, and provider.gd:29-40 documents that deletion. Remaining work is filed, not this entry: BL-0651 (the awareness reserve has no writer) and BL-0142 (sea_capacity is readout-only). One caution for whoever picks up BL-0140/BL-0145/BL-0157: strengthening a channel is NOT decorative - it is the live path by which mind investment reaches combat, so any change to trained_stage or the catalyst role must preserve get_power_bonus reaching MENTAL_DEFENSE and MIND_TECHNIQUE_POWER, or test_mind_stat_reachability.gd goes red naming it.

Without that assertion the next refactor can reintroduce the split silently, because nothing currently compares the two.

title: UNDEFINED: the breakthrough chance has no player lever, its clamp constants are unreachable, and preparing can lower it - measured 0.25 to 0.465 across all 30 realms, so MIN_CHANCE 0.05 and MAX_CHANCE 0.95 are never produced
source: REAL, and the recorded numbers are still exact. _chance at advancement.gd:252-253 is MIN_CHANCE + clarity * CLARITY_TO_CHANCE, and training.gd:66 caps clarity at exactly source_seed.clarity_required while the gate demands clarity >= source_seed.clarity_required (advancement.gd:78, breakthrough_condition.gd:29), so at attempt time clarity IS the seed constant and chance is a per-realm constant. Across all 30 seeds clarity_required runs 0.40 to 0.83, so chance spans [0.25, 0.465] and MIN_CHANCE 0.05 and MAX_CHANCE 0.95 are unreachable - the numbers this entry recorded. Preparing can also LOWER the chance on 7 realms; that is BL-0109, not a separate defect. One correction: the chance is published by preview(), not by summary().
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL and every number re-derived off the 30 seeds and unchanged. _chance at game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/advancement.gd:293-294 is clampf(MIN_CHANCE + sea.clarity * CLARITY_TO_CHANCE, MIN_CHANCE, MAX_CHANCE) with MIN_CHANCE 0.05, MAX_CHANCE 0.95 and CLARITY_TO_CHANCE 0.5 (:34-39), and MindTraining.cultivate caps clarity at EXACTLY seed.clarity_required (training.gd:69, minf(target, ...) with nothing that overshoots) while the gate demands clarity >= source_seed.clarity_required (advancement.gd:78 area, breakthrough_condition.gd:29) - so at attempt time clarity IS the seed constant and chance is a per-realm constant. Re-measured across all 30 seeds: clarity_required runs 0.40 to 0.83, so the produced chance spans exactly [0.25, 0.465] and NEITHER clamp bound is ever reached: 0.05 can never be produced because clarity is never 0 at the gate, and 0.95 would need clarity 1.8. Preparing can also LOWER the chance on the 7 realms whose clarity_required is below the sea's 0.5 default - that is BL-0109, one defect, not two, and fixing BL-0109 removes the perverse direction. ONE DECISION DRIVES THE WHOLE ENTRY: either (a) let clarity be pushed PAST the realm target by removing the training.gd:69 cap, so preparation buys roll and the clamp constants become reachable - note the cap is what makes 0.95 unreachable even in the best case, since max authored clarity_required is 0.83 -> 0.465; or (b) admit chance is authored per realm, and delete CLARITY_TO_CHANCE and both clamps as pretence, which also means deleting the false docstring at :36-39 that justifies the clamp with a rule that is not why it is there. Then RENDER it either way: the number already exists - preview publishes chance (mind_cultivation_screen.gd:58 consumes it) and no row shows it, so a player sees a gate they cannot influence and never sees the number. Do not do (a) and BL-0109's cap fix in one change: they touch the same line, and separating them is what tells you which one moved the chance.

title: PARTIAL: the once-only award is sound, but attempt identity and roll-seed machinery is unproven - sequence and rng_state are serialized and nothing asserts either, and attempt ids collide when sequence is lost
source: NOW TWO THIRDS COVERED, so the entry as written is stale. The id round trip is asserted at test_mind_persistence.gd:145 and test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:363 and :392; a reloaded attempt resolving to the recorded seed outcome is asserted at test_mind_persistence.gd:165-167; and rng_state and sequence are asserted equal in the serialized payload by the loop at test_mind_persistence.gd:249-253, so dropping either from serialization cannot survive. What is still unasserted: that two attempts on ONE actor receive DIFFERENT ids, which is the collision this entry predicted.
next: NARROWED TO ONE ASSERTION 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger); the other two thirds are closed and were already closed when this entry said they were not. CONFIRMED PRESENT: the id round trip at game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_mind_persistence.gd:145 and test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:363,392; a reloaded attempt resolving to its recorded seed outcome at test_mind_persistence.gd:165-167 (rng.seed = committed.rng_state); rng_state kept at test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:204; and both sequence and rng_state asserted equal in the serialized payload by test_mind_persistence.gd:249-253, so dropping either from serialization cannot survive. WHAT IS STILL UNASSERTED IS EXACTLY ONE THING: that two attempts on ONE actor receive DIFFERENT ids. The mechanism is real and I read it at the source - game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/advancement.gd:405-407 _next_sequence returns previous.sequence + 1 (or 1 when there is no previous), and game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/attempt.gd:97-99 make_id is a pure function of actor id, path id and sequence, so the ids CANNOT collide while sequence increments and WILL collide the moment sequence is lost or reset. The existing test proves the opposite direction: test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:184-187 asserts a second start is REFUSED while one is active, which is why nothing catches the collision. ONE TEST TO ADD, mirroring the body suite verbatim: game/tests/modules/body_cultivation/test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:171-197 already asserts first sequence 1, id-is-a-pure-function, and second sequence 2 after a cancel. Add the mind twin - two starts on one actor must differ in attempt_id and the second must carry sequence 2 - and it dies if _next_sequence ever stops advancing. DO IT BEFORE BL-0151 publishes the lifecycle: publishing start/resolve/cancel to production exposes the collision to a player instead of to a fixture, which is the whole reason this entry was filed before that one.

title: PARTIAL: the breakthrough award magnitude is unconstrained - changing will 2.0 to will 10.0 at all 30 realms leaves the suite green
source: REAL, and the cause is a tautology rather than a missing assertion. test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:223 asserts will == before + _award(seed), where _award at :108-112 SUMS the same seed.rewards dictionary that advancement.gd:402-404 awards from, so any retune of the authored magnitude satisfies the assertion by construction. test_full_traversal.gd:182 asserts only awarded == (will > will_before). Nothing anywhere pins 2.0, which is consistent with the recorded control mutation.
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL, and the cause is still a tautology rather than a missing assertion. game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:239 asserts will == before + _award(seed), where _award at :108-112 SUMS the same seed.rewards dictionary that advancement.gd:464-466 awards from - so ANY retune of the authored magnitude satisfies the assertion by construction, and the recorded control mutation (will 2.0 -> 10.0 at all 30 realms, suite stays green) follows from that arithmetic rather than from a gap. test_full_traversal.gd:182 asserts only awarded == (will > will_before). Nothing anywhere pins 2.0: I re-measured all 30 seeds and the set of distinct reward values has cardinality 1, so there is no second data point in the content for a test to learn from either. FIX: assert the magnitude against a number the TEST owns - an expected table, or an explicit per-realm constant - once per realm in the traversal suite, so a retune has to be argued instead of absorbed. That is deliberately duplicating authored data in the test, and the duplication is the point: a generator-parity assertion would NOT do it (tools/cultivation/seed_systems.py writes the same 2.0, so parity is satisfied by any value the generator and the seeds agree on - the tautology again, one layer up). ANSWER IT WITH BL-0115, which is the balance question the same number raises: until an owner rules whether the award should differentiate with depth, this assertion pins a value nobody has defended.

title: sect and nation are a shared three-tier vocabulary, not two parallel hierarchies
next: Write the base ADR: clan=born to, sect=sworn to, nation=lives under. One claim shape (position + standing + obligation) in both, authored once in contracts/, so a promotion rule is written once and read by both. Blocks every item below.

title: sect module: register, scaffold and facade skeleton
next: tools new_module sect; deps contracts+core+clan. Mirror the destiny 6-file shape (state/def/catalog/gate/projection/api) with an empty authored catalog. No body until the vocabulary ADR lands.

title: nation module: register, scaffold and facade skeleton
next: tools new_module nation; deps contracts+core+sect. nation reads sect, never the reverse. Registered-but-absent is a warning not a failure, so the permission can land first.

title: the shared claim value object: a position, a standing and an obligation
next: One Resource-free value object in contracts/ used by both sect and nation, so rank, standing and duty are the same three fields everywhere. Zero authored .tres may bind a contracts/ script (rules.py RESOURCE_HOME_UNITS).

title: neither sect nor nation may grant a stat directly
next: The load-bearing refusal: an institution hands out recognition, access and teaching, never power. Standing multiplies what the member can already do and is applied as a bounded percent. Reject in review any design where joining raises a base stat.

title: sect founding: a member founds a sect with an authored doctrine
next: Founding consumes a documented cost and writes a roster with one founder at the top position. The founder is the first entry in the sect's own ledger, not a special case.

title: joining, leaving and expulsion are three different verbs with three different costs
next: Leaving is always permitted and always costs standing. Expulsion costs the expeller more than it costs the expelled. Collapsing them into one verb loses the whole politics layer.

title: sect roster and the authored capacity that bounds it
next: A roster is a member list with an authored cap per position. Capacity is authored data, so a sect cannot grow past its own content, and an overflow is a refused admit, not a silent trim.

title: nation founding and succession: a polity outlives the actor who made it
next: A nation persists across generations the way a clan does (ADR 0064), so founding writes a ledger with no owner and succession is an event on it rather than a death handler.

title: sect positions are duties, not levels: outer/inner/elder and what each may do
next: A position grants a set of authored duties. Reuse the clan two-part split from ADR 0064 exactly: rank is discrete and authored, standing is a continuous earned integer, and neither is derived from the other.

title: nation offices are seats that exist whether or not anyone fills them
next: An office is a named seat with authored powers and a holder that may be empty. A vacant office is a readable state, which is what makes a succession contested.

title: promotion and demotion move standing and position independently
next: Two separate verbs on purpose: standing can rise without a promotion, and a promotion can be granted on little standing. A single verb makes the hierarchy purely numeric and removes the politics ADR 0064 kept.

title: succession: a position is filled by an heir, a trial or a contest
next: Reuse the ascension-is-walked shape from ADR 0058 rather than rolling a number. The method is authored per position, so a sect can name its heir and a nation can run a trial.

title: territory is an authored region with an owner, not a coordinate
next: Territory does not reuse world locations (ADR 0045): a location is a place, a territory is a claim over places. Author TerritoryDef with its own catalog and no overlap with WorldLocationDef's danger/resources fields.

title: claiming, holding and releasing a territory
next: Three verbs with different costs. A claim needs a holder with standing; a release is always allowed; a claim on a held territory is a conflict, not an overwrite.

title: territory yield and upkeep, paid on a clock that does not exist yet
next: Yield per period against an upkeep cost. DEF-0111 records that there is no calendar or world tick, so this item is blocked on a clock and must not invent a second one.

title: contested territory: a claim on held ground produces a conflict, never a silent flip
next: The conflict is data describing two parties and a prize. It hands off to the conflict resolution item rather than resolving itself, so one module owns how a conflict ends.

title: doctrine is an authored practice a sect exists to teach
next: A doctrine names what the sect teaches and what it refuses. Authored in SectDef so adding a school of thought is a .tres, and two sects with the same doctrine are rivals, not duplicates.

title: affinity is the fit between a member and the sect's doctrine, and it gates teaching
next: Affinity is fit, not loyalty and not a stat. It rises with teaching and falls with contradictory practice, and it gates who may be taught - never what the member is worth.

title: teaching spends the teacher and is refused when affinity is too low
next: A teach verb with a real cost on the teacher, refused with a named reason below the authored floor. Teaching that is free and unlimited makes disciples a resource faucet.

title: technique library access: a sect holds manuals its members may read
next: Blocked on the technique-access contracts seam, NOT on techniques. TechniquesApi is at exactly 12 public methods (MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS), so the sect cannot be given a verb on it; and TechniqueGate is not the only path to a CodexEntry (1363 authored technique items route to ItemActivation.LEARNED). The seam must be a contracts/ interface shaped like damage_mechanism.gd (ADR 0067), reached by component id, with sect implementing it and techniques asking it. Needs its own ADR.

title: dues, tribute and patronage are authored terms, never automatic payment
next: ADR 0064 already decided a clan publishes terms and does not collect them. A sect does the same: the settlement verb belongs to a later economy, so this item authors the terms only.

title: a sect treasury is a ledger of obligations, not a pile of items
next: Hold the claims and dues as ledger lines. A treasury that duplicates the items module's inventory makes two sources of truth for what an institution owns.

title: favour and debt between institutions, symmetric like faction stance
next: Reuse the ADR 0047 symmetry rule: a favour owed by A to B is readable from both sides, so no module holds a one-sided opinion about another institution's debt.

title: inter-sect rivalry is a symmetric stance between sects, not a hostility list
next: Same shape as WorldFactionDef.relationships (ADR 0047) and the same authoring story: changing a stance is editing a .tres, and it is always symmetric.

title: inter-nation diplomacy: alliance, truce, embargo, war
next: A closed verb set on a symmetric stance. An unknown verb refuses closed and names itself, following the DestinyGate precedent rather than defaulting to neutral.

title: a sect or nation conflict resolves through the one combat spine, never its own formula
next: Blocked on nothing in the module: the declare/count/pay half is built and tested (--suite nation). What is missing is the PRODUCER of verdicts. Ship `contest` succession content only once a tournament can call advance_succession; ADR 0085 rules that an authored-but-unreachable method is dead content, the same failure ADR 0063 shipped as unreachable tiers.

title: war resolution and spoils, including a defeated institution's standing
next: A resolved conflict pays a prize and moves standing on both sides. Losing standing must be recoverable, so a defeat lowers a number rather than dissolving the institution.

title: schism and secession: a sect can split, and the split costs both halves
next: Being built: SectApi.declare_schism costs both halves.

title: sect and nation NPCs: institutions that act without the player
next: Blocked on DEF-0111 (no clock). Institution simulation needs a season. The seam is decided: app/ owns real time and calls into the module with an explicit periods count; a module must never grow its own timer, because a second clock is a second source of truth for when a save happened. Do NOT build this until a clock exists.

title: the faction relation graph reads sect and nation stances without owning them
next: Being built: a read-only relations module that stores no stance.

title: reputation toward a sect or nation is separate from standing inside it
next: Being built: the sect screen as a pure read of SectApi.summary.

title: sect screen: a pure read of the facade with no rules of its own
next: Being built: the nation screen as a board of offices.

title: nation screen: the polity as a board of offices rather than a list of numbers
next: Blocked on BL-0201 and a quest system (BL-0053). The five states (found/built/contested/lost/rebuilt) can be authored now as a state machine with authored gates and needs no quest system to be testable; only the CONTENT is blocked.

title: the founder's arc: found, build, lose and rebuild, as a quest-shaped progression
next: A reachability guard for authored sect/nation content: every authored position, office, doctrine and succession method must be reachable by some authored path. ADR 0063 shipped dead tiers because nothing asserted reachability, so the guard is a test beside realm_power check, not a comment.

title: authored content for sects, nations and territories ships as .tres with no code
next: Every def is a Resource under game/data/. A sect, nation or territory that needs code to add one has the wrong shape. tools data audit gates the cross-references.

title: a reachability guard: no authored position, office or doctrine may be unreachable
next: ADR 0063 shipped dead tiers because nothing asserted the numbers were reachable. Assert every authored position is grantable by some path, or the content is decoration.

title: contract tests for both facades, one suite per concern
next: Needs its own ADR before the first authored .tres ships: where a POLITY ledger lives. actor.module_data dies with the actor, and a nation outlives the actor that founded it (ADR 0083). Tracked as DEF-0119. The first slice uses module_data and the ledger is JSON-safe; a screen built before this is answered would be a screen rewrite.

title: the sect and nation save schema is JSON-safe and versioned per ledger
next: ADR 0027 module_data is String-keyed and JSON-round-tripped in a test. An institution ledger holding an Actor or a Resource ref silently breaks every save.

title: RATE_STEP guard asserts a pasted 1.05, not the invariant it claims (VACUOUS guard)
source: orchestrator review 2026-10-03, after ADR 0066 collapsed the rate into core/realm_rate.gd
next: AGENTS.md states the invariant as: RATE_STEP must stay at or below the smallest per-realm step in the authored work budget, or the rate outruns the price and the deep realms get cheap. But game/tests/core/test_realm_rate.gd:78 asserts the literal RealmRate.RATE_STEP <= 1.05, and AGENTS.md notes tools realm_power check does not cover RATE_STEP at all. A pasted bound cannot detect the thing it is standing in for: if a realm seed's work_required steps shrink, the invariant can be violated while the test still passes. Replace the literal with a computed check against the smallest per-realm ratio in the authored work budget - the same drift-detecting shape the seed generator already has.

title: ADR 0067's 11-stage damage spine is Accepted in docs and implemented nowhere
source: orchestrator review 2026-10-03; combat api.gd is 16 lines with 2 public methods
next: Stage 0 of the Domain program, because AC5 (a domain you can fight in) is unreachable without it. Build modules/combat/combat_damage.gd with S1-S11 in ADR 0067's stated order, contracts/damage_mechanism.gd as the seam, CombatTuning in combat_damage.tres, and DamageProposal as {amount: float, effects: Array[Dictionary]}. Then the qi, body and mind mechanisms from ADR 0069/0070/0071. Four orderings must be independently assertable: S1 before S2 (the ladder must not move hit frequency), S2 before S4 (a miss invokes no mechanism), S4 before S6 (crit multiplies the mechanism's output and is never its input), and S7 before S8 before S9 (reduction runs, then the floor restores the chip). No rounding anywhere and no division in the spine.

title: PlayerAdapter.attack() is a comment, so nothing the player does in a domain resolves
next: PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-10-03, re-scope before working: PlayerAdapter.attack() is no longer a comment - it has a real body (requires State.COMBAT and a Node2D target). But it is not the domain-fight path and should not be made one: the shipped fight runs through CombatApi.exchange, which resolves the player's offense into a share of the boss's authored vitality and spends it with LootApi.strike. PlayerAdapter.attack targets a spatial Node2D, and there is no spatial layer yet (see BL-0212), so it is a world-interaction verb waiting on the world, not a missing damage source. Do not wire it to the domain fight.

next: Grow DomainDef into a map description - layout (handcrafted scene id OR template id plus seed), rooms, paths, actor spawn refs, fixtures and environment - behind one producer interface so a handcrafted and a generated domain are indistinguishable downstream. 160 .tres already exist and stay valid: every new field is optional and a def that omits them keeps today's behaviour. Also extend tools data audit with the new kinds and cross-references; data.py:112,235 hardcodes the domain schema and script path today. || SHIPPED 2026-10-03, verified 53 passing in test_domain_map_contract: the domain module owns the map model. RoomDef, DomainMap, EnvironmentZoneDef, DomainRoles and DomainMapContract exist; DomainMap is engine-agnostic and JSON-clean; entering a map that fails the contract is refused by name (DomainApi.enter -> ERR_INVALID_CONTRACT). title: CLOSED by BL-0428 plus 7594d37b: unique routes have one owner; the duplicate set_id column is gone and its guard was tautological until that commit
next:
VERIFIED ON THE CURRENT TREE BY A DISPATCHED AGENT, then re-checked by root. Read this as closure with a caveat, not as an unbroken claim.

BL-0231 IS FIXED. The entry described a top tier unsatisfiable because its ceiling was a member COUNT rather than a placement. The historical ladder (recoverable at c0ab2689) ended 2,3,4,5,6 with the capstone declared as count 6. The current file carries 2,3,4,5 and SetDef no longer has max_equippable or unreachable_tier_indices at all; SetCatalog.max_wearable delegates to SetPlacement.placed_count, which is augmenting-path matching over real slots. A count of 6 could never be satisfiable across 5 wearable slots; a placement is. BL-0427 records the fix.

BL-0232 IS FIXED, and its guard was WEAKER THAN IT LOOKED until commit 7594d37b. The entry complained that set_bonus declares boss drop routes twice by two mechanisms nothing keeps in agreement. The historical index (recoverable at c0ab2689) carried set_id, boss_id and slot columns; the current one carries only unique_id, domain_id, route_realm, min_rarity and drop_weight, with api.gd:_set_listing deriving membership. So the duplication is gone, per BL-0428. BUT the guard that was supposed to prove it was tautological: drop_route computes boss_id from UniqueItem.route_boss_id(def) and item_subtype from def.subcategory verbatim, so the assertions were f(x) == f(x) and stayed green whether or not the runtime honoured the route. 7594d37b replaces them with a claim that carries the deletion - that LootRoutes.permits and Equipment.equip actually read the definition - and mutation-proves it six ways.

ONE RESIDUAL THAT CONTENT CANNOT DISTINGUISH, and it is worth knowing before anyone calls the invariant airtight. A max_wearable implemented as min(member_count(), SLOTS.size()) would still pass every shipped test: the void coil works out to min(6,5)=5 which equals its real placement of 5, and the other three sets have no slot contention at all. So no shipped set separates the count formula from the placement formula - the invariant rests on the unit-level ceiling test plus the end-to-end equip, not on the corpus. Closing that needs a five-member set with two members contending for one slot, which is authored content rather than a code change. Anyone strengthening this later should author that set first, or the test will keep agreeing with both implementations.

title: Byte ceiling overshoots badly at a writer faster than the incident
source: Measured with a synthetic flooder after the per-run-log refactor: killed at 0.12s having written 251 MB against a 64 MB ceiling, i.e. 187 MB overshoot, because the flooder sustained ~2 GB/s. title: Every concurrent run shared one log file, corrupting the trail and the ceiling
source: LOG_FILE was the single fixed path build/godot.log and run_godot truncated it at every start. title: A run that hangs SILENTLY defeats the byte ceiling: it writes nothing, so the disk guard cannot see it
source: Measured: 	ools test --suite mind_cultivation produced a 0-byte log for 32s+ while the engine sat at 0.1s CPU and 0MB RSS (idle, not spinning). tools/godot.py's byte ceiling measures LOG SIZE, so a silent hang is invisible to it and only the 900s wall clock catches it.

Structural roles (entry, core, gate, arena) are rule-placed; content roles (settlement, boss) are author-pinned only and never auto-placed. Floor and corridors share ONE terrain set so the room/corridor seam needs no special case; walls are the 1-cell dilation minus the rect; WallLayer.collision_enabled=true is the single physics layer; WallLayer y_sort with a centered origin so the player passes behind a wall's top edge.

title: A domain run is one more module_data key beside loot_state, and the two own disjoint truths

title: The only subtype-to-slot rule in the repo lives in ui/; gameplay enforces no slot rule at all
next: game/src/ui/panels/item_action_rules.gd:21-27 (SUBTYPE_SLOTS, ACCESSORY_SLOTS) is the ONLY subtype-to-slot map in the repo, and it lives in ui/. Gameplay has no such rule: Equipment.equip accepts any slot in Equipment.SLOTS for any is_equipment() def, so nothing at the engine level stops two same-subtype items occupying two slots. Consequence: void_serpent_coil's fang/heart weapon contest is a UI CONVENTION, not a rule - the engine would happily let a player wear both. ORCHESTRATOR RULING: the map belongs in the items module as Equipment.slots_for(def), and ui/ must read it rather than own it. This is AGENTS.md's own principle ('ui/ is a separate program from gameplay; it never owns game rules') being violated by an instance of it, and the rules hole is real independently of the architecture: two weapons is currently legal. This also unblocks a better max_equippable - the set_bonus agent notes min(member_count, SLOTS) is only an approximation because two members compete for one weapon slot, and a real bipartite matching becomes possible once the rule is engine-level. No ADR required: this moves a rule between modules and changes neither core/ nor contracts/. Needs an agent; items/ is held by the standing Item agent and ui/ is in flight, so it is deliberately NOT dispatched yet.

title: Actor needs SCHEMA_VERSION 5 and a body_attempt slot; bumping it breaks a mind test assertion

KNOWN CONFLICT: game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_mind_persistence.gd:279 asserts Actor.SCHEMA_VERSION == 4, so whoever makes the core change must update that assertion in the same change. This is a core/ change and therefore REQUIRES an ADR in the same change.

title: The three cultivation screens expose three incompatible summary() vocabularies for the same concepts
next: AGENTS.md's testable contract is 'every screen/panel exposes summary() -> Dictionary: primitives only ... Tests assert that, not pixels', but nothing requires the three cultivation screens to agree on shape, and they do not. Measured unmet vocabularies: BODY uses formatted prose - 'Progress 0/42', 'Missing breakthrough pill', 'Required channels are not trained deep enough'. QI uses snake_case codes - 'insufficient_progress', 'missing_breakthrough_item', 'channel_not_ready:lung'. MIND uses prose with a colon - 'Progress: 0/100', 'Channel lung not ready'. Related shape drift in the same summaries: body exposes actions as a flat {verb: bool} and a 'ready' flag, while qi and mind nest {actions: [...], available: [...], enabled: {verb: bool}, primary} and expose 'can_act' instead of 'ready'. Consequences: no cross-path UI assertion can be written without special-casing each screen, and a test asserting 'the pill gate is named' can string-match qi's code but must REGEX body's prose. This is also a trap for tooling - I misread body's flat actions as qi being empty, and then misread a driver error event as a null result, because the shapes differ. DECISION NEEDED (not a refactor): either the three screens adopt one shared action/gate vocabulary with path-specific payloads, or AGENTS.md states that shapes are path-specific by design and each screen documents its own contract. Either is defensible; leaving it undocumented is not, because the inconsistency has now misled a reader twice in one session.

title: CORRECTION: BL-0291 was my fourth false alarm - screens INHERIT setup from UiScreen
next: BL-0291 claimed 9 of 11 routed screens have no setup() and that navigating to them mounts a blank screen and throws. FALSE, and it was my error. My check was a text search for a line beginning with 'func setup(' in each screen's own file, which only finds a screen that OVERRIDES setup and cannot see an INHERITED one. game/src/ui/screens/ui_screen.gd line 21 declares 'var _actor: Actor = null' and line 29 declares 'func setup(actor: Actor) -> void:'. Every one of those nine screens extends UiScreen, so they all inherit setup(actor) and _actor, and in Godot an inherited method satisfies has_method('setup') and _screen.call('setup', _actor) works. Confirmed on loot_encounter.gd specifically: it never declares or assigns _actor itself and correctly inherits both. CONSEQUENCE, which is why this one matters more than the other three: I had already DISPATCHED an agent to add setup() to all nine screens. Nine redundant overrides would have been a duplicate-actor bug in nine files - exactly the hazard I warned that agent about while handing it the false premise. I have stopped it and told it to revert anything it already added. THE REAL LESSON, and it generalises past this repo: a text search cannot see inheritance, so any finding that rests on a grep which a single base-class declaration would overturn is not a finding yet. Prefer an executable probe - instantiate the node and ask has_method - over searching source. This is the fourth false alarm I have filed in one session (the others: granting the current realm's pill instead of the target realm's, a driver verb typo whose error event my formatting rendered as null, and an ungranted sea catalyst). Every one looked serious; none survived checking. The mitigations are now in the briefs I send: verify against the runtime, and check whether a gate is gated on an authored item you never granted before calling it unreachable.

That is backwards, and it trains the next author to delete the explanation rather than keep the rule. It was also a live gate failure: test_ui_conventions sat at 347 passed / 1 failed with that message. FIXED by adding a _code_only(text) helper that strips an unquoted # comment from every line before the check, so the guard reads code and not prose. Proof both ways: the suite went 347/1 -> 348/0, and a deliberate mutation adding a REAL theme_override_font_sizes property beside an existing theme_type_variation took it to 347 passed / 1 failed naming tribulation_screen.gd, then restored to 348/0. So the guard now passes a file that mentions the banned token in a comment and still fails one that uses it. GENERALISE: any convention check that greps raw source text is capable of this, and the fix is to strip comments first. Worth auditing the other text-scanning checks in tests/arch_rules and test_ui_conventions for the same failure mode - a guard that punishes good comments gets good comments deleted.

title: One half-written file made a 26,545-test run unreadable: 1070 script errors cascaded from items/api.gd failing to parse
next: Full gate run reported Results: 26545 passed / 357 failed / 158 suites AND 'fail 1070 script error(s) aborted a test mid-function; those tests reported no failure, so the run above is incomplete'. The entire cascade had ONE cause, visible in the tail of the log: res://src/modules/items/api.gd did not parse at that instant. Everything else followed from it - 'Could not resolve script res://src/modules/items/api.gd', then 'Cannot infer the type of _ITEMS constant', then 'Could not resolve class ItemsApi', then 'Static function attach_dantian() not found in base QiCultivationApi', repeated down the whole tree. VERIFIED IT WAS TRANSITENT, NOT MINE: items/api.gd is 240 lines and parses cleanly now, and its own suite is 54 passed / 0 failed (it was 46 when the save fix landed, so the owner is still working). The file's mtime was during my run. So the 357 is a contaminated reading and must NOT be recorded as the program's state - this is precisely the AGENTS.md warning that a full run mid-build reports other agents' in-flight breakage as your own. THE SYSTEMIC FINDING, which is the durable part: one agent writing a file in place makes a 26,545-test run not merely wrong but UNREADABLE, because a parse failure cascades through every dependant and aborts tests that would otherwise report their real result. There is currently no way to tell contention noise from a genuine regression at a glance. RECOMMENDED FIX, in tools/ which I own but am not doing unilaterally mid-flight: a cheap pre-flight parse of every script under res://src before the suite runs, so an unparseable file fails in one second naming the file and the line, instead of after a full run producing 1070 errors nobody can triage. Same argument as the unbounded-while guard - turn an unreadable result into a build failure.

title: DONE: tools test names the scripts that failed to LOAD, so a cascade is a diagnosis not a dump

title: A module-local substitute now duplicates ADR 0057; two sources of truth until it is resolved
next: SEQUENCING HAZARD, recorded so it is not lost between two agents. The body agent, unable to touch contracts/ or core/, shipped a module-local substitute so the body path was not left with a dead reward: BodyProvider.new(actor) holds the ACTOR rather than the network, with _invalidate_stats_on_meridian_change in body_cultivation/api.gd, and provider.gd's _meridian_power_bonus now reads the injected actor. Meanwhile ADR 0057 prescribes a context accessor that is being restored right now by a separate agent. THE HAZARD: for as long as both exist there are TWO answers to how a provider reaches the meridian network, and the one that works today is the one that will be deleted. A future agent reading provider.gd will see a working pattern that contradicts the ADR. RESOLUTION IS A DECISION, not a cleanup: either the substitute is removed once the accessor lands and provider.gd goes back to reading context.meridian_network(), or the substitute becomes permanent and ADR 0057 is SUPERSEDED (ADRs are immutable - supersede, never rewrite), which also settles what contracts/attack_context.gd does when it has no network to pass. Until one of those happens, a stat that is quietly 0 is the failure mode ADR 0057 exists to prevent. Do not let this sit: it is the same shape as the deleted 'value' field, the unloaded meridian .tres files, and the numeraire's fabricated source - a gate green-lighting a second authority.

title: A bare while true: made GDScript's analyzer reject the file, zeroing a 407-line suite: the last unloadable suite in the repo
source: tools test, session 2026-10-03: 47 script errors reduced to 1, and that one was 'Not all code paths return a value' at test_nation_conflict.gd:347
next: FIXED, and the class is now structurally impossible. Cause: _names_a_type() in test_nation_conflict.gd was while true: with only eturns inside. GDScript's flow analysis cannot PROVE a while true: returns, so it emitted 'Not all code paths return a value' and refused to compile the file -- taking a 407-line suite to zero assertions. It was the last unloadable suite and the only parse error left in a 248-suite run. The loop was not actually unbounded (from advances past every hit and find returns -1 past the end of line), so this was purely the analyzer, not a spin. Fix: the search window became the bound -- while from <= line.length(): with  reak on the not-found case and a definite eturn false after -- so the condition states what terminates it, matching AGENTS.md. Before 0 assertions, after Results: 187 passed, 3 failed. Swept and hardened the only two other bare while true: in the repo, both in traversal suites (body_cultivation and qi_cultivation), by moving an existing guard <= 64 cap from the loop body into the condition; both still report 492/0 and 440/0, and the repo-wide unbounded-wait guard is 699 passed, 0 failed. Repo-wide count of bare while true: is now 0. Worth knowing for the future: a while true: is not merely a style problem in GDScript, it is a compile error whenever the enclosing function declares a return type, so one loop can silently zero out an entire suite.

title: The teaching door is circular: the only writer of fit is the verb that refuses you for lacking fit, so no student can ever be taught
source: tools test --suite sect/test_sect_teaching, session 2026-10-03: Results: 66 passed, 12 failed; exhaustive grep for fit writers across game/src
next: CIRCULAR GATE, proven by exhaustive search of fit writers -- the same class as BL-0106 (nothing starts a tribulation, so R19+ is a wall). Chain: SectApi.teach checks SectTeaching.student_admitted(def, s_ledger), which is def.teaches_at(SectState.fit(student_ledger, def.doctrine_id)), which is student_fit >= def.min_purity. The ONLY production writer of a ledger fit map is SectTeaching.apply_fit (grep for apply_fit across game/src returns exactly one caller, api.gd:484, inside teach). sect_state.gd:313 writes fit too, but that is SectState.normalize -- save-payload normalization on attach, not a verb that grants anything. So the one thing that raises fit is the verb that refuses you for lacking it: a student below the door can never be taught, and therefore can never rise above the door. The suite proves it the only way it can, by hand-writing the ledger: test_sect_teaching.gd:260 and :273 assign (ledger['fit'])[DOCTRINE] directly and re-attach, which is the test doing the player's job -- the same anti-pattern as BL-0101. Measured: 12 failures, 11 of them this (every ordinary-student case refuses with standing_below_floor; the 12th asserts the door itself). Authored doors are real, not fixture noise: game/data min_purity is 10 for the foundry fixture and 30 for iron_vine. Two fixes, and they are NOT equivalent, so this needs a deliberate choice rather than a patch: (a) read the student's STANDING at the door instead of fit -- supported by the reason string already being STANDING_BELOW_FLOOR, by the doctrine's own words 'a member under it is not being taught anything', and by standing being reachable through join and SectApi.move_standing; or (b) keep the fit door and grant fit at join or founding, so the first lesson can land. (a) makes the door reachable with no new content and makes the existing reason string honest; (b) preserves fit as the door but needs an authored grant. Separately worth fixing either way: the reason for a FIT refusal is named standing_below_floor, so a panel would tell a player their standing is too low when their affinity is -- a vocabulary lie in the direction ADR 0083 says is load-bearing for every screen.

title: All 27 domain_generator failures are one cause: every authored room pin is silently dropped, and a complete pin would only half-apply
source: tools test --suite domain/test_domain_generator, session 2026-10-03; all 27 messages reduce to 'placed at least one author pin: expected true, got false' plus its downstream room assertions
next:
FIXED -- all 27 failures closed, suite is Results: 2018 passed, 0 failed. My earlier two write-ups on this were wrong and are superseded; the cause was three separate defects, none of which was the one I first guessed. Measured with a temporary per-seed diagnostic (leaves count, the reserved set, the settlement-kind count, and both pin dictionaries) that I then removed and restored the file around byte-identically (sha 8F66E072DFB2).
(1) DATA. game/src/data/domains/templates/flame_valley_depths.tres authored pin_camp with room_def = ExtResource 5_camp (ash_camp.tres) but its room_pool was only [2_floor, 3_chamber, 6_furnace] -- 5_camp was missing. _pinned_defs checks pool membership and _fail()s, so that pin was un-honourable on EVERY seed: 64 of the 77 failures were this one template across seeds 1..64. The sibling stormwrack_reach.tres does list 5_camp, which is what made it obvious. Fixed by adding ExtResource("5_camp") to that pool. 27 -> 15 failures.
(2) CODE. _place_structural built reserved = [entry, core, gate] + arenas with no budget, so it could cover EVERY leaf: ember_grotto seed 46 produced leaves=8 reserved=[1,5,2,0,3,4,6,7], _free_leaf answered -1, and the pin was dropped with no diagnostic -- the exact outcome _pinned_defs own docstring says must not happen. The same line also admitted duplicates and -1 (flame_valley seed 49 gave reserved=[7,7,-1]), because the three indexes come from three different searches and _lowest_neighbour can answer -1. Fixed: reserved is built deduplicated and non-negative, and arena_budget = leaves - reserved - pins, so a pin always has a leaf to land on. Arenas are the discretionary kind and give way; floor/core/gate do not, because a pin is documented never to overrule geometry. 15 -> 10 failures.
(3) CODE. kinds[core] = &"core" is guarded on core != entry, and _farthest answers the entry whenever the entry is its own farthest -- routine for a shallow or single-branch map -- so those maps had NO core room at all. Fixed with a deterministic fallback to the lowest canonical non-entry index, the same rule-not-a-roll shape as _entry_index. 10 -> 0 failures.
MUTATION PROOF, both code fixes load-bearing: disabling the core fallback gives 2008 passed / 10 failed naming exactly "every generated domain has one core"; removing pins from arena_budget gives 1996 passed / 5 failed naming exactly the pin-starvation messages including ember_grotto seed 46. One fix I tried and REVERTED: adding the pool check to _apply_pins and _pinned_kinds so a kind can never be placed without its def. It is correct in principle but made things worse (27 -> 77) because it turned defect (1) into "nothing placed at all" on flame_valley; the real fix there was the data, not a third guard. Left that file untouched.

title: BLOCKER: WorldAnchor.commit has zero production callers, so no ascent is ever begun and R29-R30 is unreachable
source: orchestrator, measured by driving the shipped panel 2026-10-03
next: CIRCULARITY REFUTED - MY EARLIER READING WAS WRONG, recorded here so nobody re-files it. breakthrough.gd:201-206 ascension_ok opens with 'if next_index <= WorldAnchor.COMMIT_MICRO: return true'. COMMIT_MICRO is 27 (world_anchor.gd:29). So entering index 27 is checked by ascension_ok(actor,27) -> 27 <= 27 -> TRUE, no ascent owed; that advance then commits 27 and begins the ascent; the gate that consumes it is ascension_ok(actor,28) on the NEXT advance. The commit for index N serves the gate for index N+1, never the gate on the same advance, so committing AFTER can_advance is correct and not circular. Corroboration is already in the file: inside_world_ok's docstring at breakthrough.gd:177-181 describes this exact circularity being fixed once before for R19 - 'Entering R19 commits the Seed inside world, so R19 must not require it as a prerequisite - that was circular and left the gate permanently unsatisfiable' - and ascension_ok carries the same escape hatch for the same reason. MY 'No ascent begun' DRIVE WAS MY OWN INSTRUMENT'S FAULT: realm:<id> writes state.rank_id directly and so TELEPORTS the rank, bypassing the very breakthrough into index 27 that commits. A hero teleported to 28 has correctly never begun an ascent. That is BL-0313 in a new form - the instrument jumped a gate rather than walking it. The correct instrument is Breakthrough.try_advance, which is what the Breakthrough press calls, and game/tests/core/test_player_walks_to_r30.gd uses it and contains no WorldAnchor.commit at all, only the COMMIT_MICRO constant. KEEP the core commit: it fixes no reachable bug today, but it makes the milestone have exactly one owner instead of one per caller, which is the ADR 0066 failure mode AGENTS.md exists to prevent.

title: SCOPED DOWN TO ONE BUILD: all three headline claims are false; what remains is a quest subsystem (3076 items, 1697 naming quests that do not exist)
next:
THE HEADLINE NUMBER DOES NOT DECIDE ANYTHING, and re-deriving it says WAVE 4 is ONE missing edge rather than two missing subsystems. Both facts were measured this session from the corpus and from the reader that consumes it, because three quoted numbers in this backlog measured to zero when re-derived.

FIRST: THE 442 DANGLING QUEST IDS ARE NOT A DEFECT AND CANNOT BECOME ONE. ItemSources.KINDS declares quest as {"ref": REF_OPTIONAL, "shipped": false}, and _satisfy returns NO_SHIPPED_ROUTE the moment is_shipped(kind) is false - BEFORE it looks at ref, and before it consults the injected probe. So a quest:<id> naming nothing resolvable and a quest:<id> naming a real quest produce the identical answer. The "1697 items name one of 442 quest ids no QuestDef defines" is true as a count and inert as a finding: all 442 are dangling, and that fact is not read by anything. This is the fifth instance of quoting a scan result without asking what the number means to the code that consumes it, and the most expensive one, because WAVE 4 was scoped on it.

SECOND: gather IS SHIPPED, so half of WAVE 4 does not exist. 2412 items declare gather, KINDS marks it shipped: true, and ItemSources own comment records when it changed: "gather was in this list until the forage route shipped, and the flag moved only when there was a verb behind it." ForageApi.harvest exists at forage/api.gd:184, forage declares holdings as a dependency for the granter, and the verb refuses loudly rather than accruing yield it cannot grant. The objective line "gather (2428 items) declare NO runtime route" is false as of the shipped gather route.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING, and it is one edge. QuestGrants.pay records an item grant as UNSPENT on purpose: "ItemsApi is not a quest dependency and this module does not declare one, so calling it would be an undeclared edge." Confirmed structurally - quest declares deps [contracts, core] in tools/arch/registry.json, so quest may not legally name ItemsApi. And the delivery verb ALREADY EXISTS among the frozen twelve: ItemsApi.generate(actor, def, seed_value) realizes a def from a seeded roll and acquires it into the inventory. So the fix is not a new subsystem and not a facade change; it is (a) registry: add items to quest deps, (b) QuestGrants.pay calls ItemsApi.generate for an item grant instead of recording it, (c) KINDS flips quest to shipped: true, (d) app/ supplies the quest probe that was previously unnecessary.

THE ORDER MATTERS, and it is the trap. Flipping shipped to true BEFORE the delivery edge exists would make 1697 items claim a route that grants nothing - the ADR 0065 failure this file already names for fates. The dangling 442 only become load-bearing at step (c), because that is the first moment the ref is read at all. They must be resolved or re-pointed as part of the same slice, and note what they appear to be: ids like A10_immortal_axletree_line and A12_immortal_backstaff_line name MATERIAL LINES, not quests. A bare &"quest" with no id is the honest spelling for a quest-sourced item; quest:<material-line> reads as a content line that was given the quest prefix by mistake. KINDS already permits a bare quest (REF_OPTIONAL) and already forbids a ref on gather (REF_FORBIDDEN), so the vocabulary is right and only the 1697 refs are wrong. That is a content decision about which of two spellings 1697 items meant, and it needs the ADR the boundary move requires.

title: An agent made a 3561-path blanket commit 'commit all stale src codes', violating the per-slice scoped-commit rule; net effect protective but the state committed is unreviewed

title: A test that could not fail: the discarded-network test never warmed the cache, so a lazy capture grabbed the NEW network and passed
source: body_cultivation agent, found and fixed during the ADR 0057 substitute removal, 2026-10-03
next: A GENUINE TEST DEFECT, found by the agent that removed the last ADR 0057 substitute, and worth keeping because the SHAPE recurs across this program. The test game/tests/modules/body_cultivation/test_body_meridian_read.gd::test_the_provider_never_serves_a_network_the_actor_discarded asserts a provider never serves a meridian network the actor discarded after a save/load. Under mutation M3 - capturing the network on first read instead of resolving it per read - IT STAYED GREEN, 28 passed / 0 failed. Root cause: the test never warmed the stats cache before swapping actor.meridians, so a lazy first read happened AFTER the swap and therefore grabbed the NEW network, which is the correct answer for the wrong reason. A test that only ever reads before the state it is testing has not actually tested the transition. The fix was to add a warm read before the swap - the realistic shape, since stats are computed and then the network is restored underneath - and re-applying M3 now fails on 'and not the one it discarded: expected false, got true'. GENERAL LESSON, which is why this is filed rather than closed: a test that exercises a RESTORE must perform a READ BEFORE the restore, or it is asserting nothing about the restore. The same shape produced BL-0285 (inventory capacity serialized but never restored, undetected for want of a mutation), BL-0123/0124/0125 (three body gates whose deletion left the suite green) and the tautological test_realm_rate.gd. Whenever the property under test is 'the new value is picked up', the test must establish an OLD value first.

title: The {} summary sentinel is overloaded: a screen bound with nothing supplied is indistinguishable from a screen with no actor
source: orchestrator, by driving all 16 routed screens 2026-10-03
next: THE {} SUMMARY SENTINEL IS OVERLOADED, so a screen that is bound but has nothing supplied reports IDENTICALLY to a screen with no actor at all. Found by driving all 16 routed screens rather than reading them. WHAT I MEASURED: 16 screens are routed in game/src/app/screen_routes.gd. Driving each with --path body --fresh --cmd refresh, 12 returned a populated summary (loot_encounter 38 keys, nation 26, body_cultivation_panel 24, sect 24, mind on its own path 25, qi on its own path 20, tribulation 20, destiny 19, technique_loadout 18, technique_codex 16, item_workbench 15, character 10, crafting 10, world_map 7) and 4 returned {}. I CHECKED MY OWN INSTRUMENT FIRST and was wrong twice. qi_cultivation_screen and mind_cultivation_screen bind perfectly on --path qi and --path mind respectively (20 and 25 keys) - I had driven all sixteen with --path body, so those two were my error. set_bonus_screen and socket_forge are different: BOTH extend UiScreen and therefore INHERIT setup(actor), which is exactly the inheritance trap this session has already cost two false alarms. The composition root binds them with extra shapes my driver does not perform - item_workbench_app.gd:301-306 does screen.call(setup, _actor) AND screen.call(apply_snapshot, SetBonusApi.inspect(_actor)) for ROUTE_SET_BONUS, and :280-282 does screen.call(setup, _actor) AND _forge.bind(screen) for ROUTE_SOCKET, while socket_forge.gd additionally exposes bind_view(view: Dictionary). So all sixteen screens ARE bindable and the driver is the thing that cannot bind four of them. THE REAL FINDING IS UNDERNEATH THAT: the UI standard says summary() returns {} when there is NO ACTOR, and every screen honours that. But a screen that IS bound and has been handed no snapshot also returns {}, because it has nothing to render. Those are different states - not enrolled, versus enrolled with nothing to show - and they render identically, so neither a player nor a headless test can tell them apart. That is the same class as the mind anchor gate reading open when it should read shut, and the same class as a refusal rendering like an offer: a state that is invisible because it is indistinguishable from another. Three questions nobody has decided, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: (1) should the {} sentinel be reserved strictly for no-actor, with a bound-but-empty screen reporting a distinct shape such as bound:true with an empty row list? (2) is apply_snapshot the right seam at all, or should a set-bonus screen read its snapshot through the facade like every other screen reads its state? (3) does the same overload affect any OTHER screen that renders from a pushed-in view rather than from the actor - socket forge and the workbench both qualify, and the workbench summary returned 15 keys so it is probably fine, but nobody has checked systematically. FIX FOR MY OWN INSTRUMENT, which I will do: game/tools/ui_driver.gd needs to perform the same three extra binding shapes the composition root performs, so a screen is driven exactly as the game drives it. A driver that binds a subset of what production binds will keep reporting live features as dead - which is how BL-0320 was filed against the loot screen when the fault was the harness.
