title: test_item_pipeline claims a boss drop and equips THAT, but 4 assertions fail after the claim
next:
THE TEST FAILS 83 PERCENT OF THE TIME FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT A DEFECT, and no hunt budget can fix that. The arithmetic decides it, so it is computed rather than asserted. Rate is the measured 176 of 7817 entry-band rolled entries (2.25 percent); drops per fight is the measured 2 (a real boot minted 2 rewards with 2 drops pending). Each drop is treated as ONE roll, which is conservative - a drop can carry several entries, so the true failure rate is somewhat lower than the figures below, but never lower than "most of the time".

  hunts  ~rolls  P(no wearable gear)   what that means for a mutation target
      1       2           95.6%        almost always red for a non-defect
      2       4           91.3%        almost always red for a non-defect
      4       8           83.4%        <- the configuration actually in the test
      8      16           69.5%        almost always red for a non-defect
     16      32           48.3%        too flaky to attribute a failure
     32      64           23.3%        too flaky to attribute a failure
     64     128            5.4%        still too flaky

WHY THAT DISQUALIFIES IT AS A PROOF. Criterion 9 asks for a load-bearing end-to-end that is mutation-tested, so breaking the implementation must turn it RED. A test that is already red 83 percent of the time cannot attribute a failure: when it goes red you cannot tell a broken pipeline from an unlucky draw, and when it goes green you cannot tell a working pipeline from a lucky one. That is not a weak proof, it is not a proof.

PATIENCE IS PROVABLY THE WRONG FIX, which is the finding worth keeping. Reaching P below 5 percent needs about 65 hunts, and each one is a real fight driven through the real UI. Raising MAX_HUNTS does not buy determinism; it buys a slow coin flip. The same curve where every grade passes the gate and only gear-versus-material matters (16 percent of entries are gear) gives 6.1 percent at 8 hunts and 1.5 percent at 12 - better, still not zero.

THE FIX IS TO ESTABLISH THE PRECONDITION INSTEAD OF WAITING FOR IT. Concretely: read the authored entry-band tables, find one that actually contains a grade=mortal wearable item, assert that it does as part of the setup, then drive the loot screens domain selector to the encounter bound to that table and fight there. The draw then has a known-good outcome and the assertion is about the pipeline. This is also criterion 6 done properly - a gate that is satisfiable from a legal prior state is one the test ESTABLISHES and asserts, not one it hopes to stumble into. That also explains why BL-0625 and this entry are the same defect seen twice: the bands do not aim at anything, so a test that hunts cannot be deterministic and content cannot be relied on.

THE COMMENT AND THE CODE CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, which is worth naming because it is why this sat unnoticed. The block above the loop argues the right thing - "asserting the drop is wearable after a single hunt would be asserting a fact about the corpus rather than about the pipeline" - and then implements the corpus-dependent wait it just argued against, capped at 4. The reasoning is sound and the implementation does not follow it. Recorded so whoever fixes it does not have to rediscover that the intent was already correct.

Not fixed here: game/tests/app/test_item_pipeline.gd was claimed for this pass but the engine lock was held by a live session for the whole turn, so no suite could be run and a proof that cannot be run is not a proof. Claim released rather than left held against work that did not land.

title: tools check can never reach green: ruff format cannot fix the long string literals that ruff check rejects as E501
source: measured tools lint exit 1 with 8 E501, plus a temp-file proof that uff format leaves a 127-char string at 127 while uff check reports E501 (127 > 100); session 2026-10-03
next: STRUCTURAL GATE FLAW, not 8 typos. tools check runs `fmt --check -> lint` in that order. tools/fmt.py:50 runs `ruff format`, and tools/lint.py:32 runs `ruff check tools`. pyproject.toml sets [tool.ruff] line-length = 100. `ruff format` will NOT split a string literal, but `ruff check` still reports E501 on it, so there exist lines that fmt provably cannot fix and lint provably rejects -- which means `tools check` is STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO REACH GREEN while any string in tools/ exceeds 100 chars. PROOF: wrote a single 127-char string literal to a temp file, ran `uv run ruff format`, then `uv run ruff check --select E501`; the format pass left it at 127 and the check reported `E501 Line too long (127 > 100)`. MEASURED: tools lint exits 1 with 8 E501, all in tools/map_assets.py (lines 77, 95, 113, 131, 317, 495) and tools/map_generate.py (lines 289, 311); offending line lengths are 101-104 chars, just over the limit. The offenders are long descriptive prose (asset description strings) and one argparse help string. Both files were last committed 44 and 61 minutes ago by map-generation work, so they may still be in flight and are NOT this session's to wrap unilaterally. NOT FIXED HERE DELIBERATELY: the two available fixes are (a) wrap the 8 literals, which treats the symptom and will recur for the next author who writes a long description, and (b) raise line-length or ignore E501, which is loosening a threshold and needs argued justification plus a call from whoever owns the toolchain. The real fix is a decision about which rules the linter is allowed to enforce, not an edit to map_assets.py. NEXT: an owner decides whether tools/lint.py should run the formatter-compatible rule set (in which case E501 is dropped because the formatter already governs width) or whether long prose strings get wrapped by convention; then either the 8 lines are wrapped or the lint rule set changes, and the choice gets an ADR because it changes what the gate can ever say.

title: ADR 0109 race gate was enforced on bypassable facade wrappers; it now lives in the advancement layer every caller passes
source: fixed by agent bg-2-0a560b03, verified by orchestrator

title: ADR 0062's anti-convergence claim is decorative: commonborn tops all three axes under the test's own metric, and the cap that permits it was invented in the test file
source: lineage program design audit 2026-10-03, independently recomputed from the .tres files
next: ADR 0062's load-bearing balance claim is that 'race x path is a partition, not a tier list' and that no race is best at everything. Recomputing the shipped content with the shipped metric (game/tests/modules/race/test_race_content.gd:194 _axis_strength) gives commonborn leading ALL THREE axes - QI 1.04, BODY 1.04, MIND 1.04 - because it closes mind (scored -1000), has no realm ceiling, carries a 36500-day lifespan and gives +1.0 to all seven base attributes, while the three specialists give 2-4 on one attribute and nothing elsewhere. commonborn is also the fallback every raceless actor is born into (ADR 0108: 'no actor is ever born raceless'), so the default body is the strongest body. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS: (1) the threshold is a test-file invention - MAX_TOP_AXES := 2 at test_race_content.gd:19 - and grepping all 111 ADRs for 'top-2'/'two axes'/'more than one axis' finds zero hits, so the test asserts a rule no ADR states; (2) a metric that scores a closed path as -1000 cannot express a body plan, because 'leading an axis you are forbidden to enter' is an artifact of the scoring function rather than a balance property. THE FIX, and it is the one ADR 0062 actually cares about: delete the scoring metric and assert the STRUCTURAL claim instead - every authored race must be refused at least one breakthrough by ADR 0109's gate. That is what the partition means, it is already implemented, and it cannot be gamed by a constant. commonborn will still need a realm ceiling or a narrower affinity set, because as shipped the body everyone is born into is the widest, the longest-lived of the non-stoneborn, and the numerically best on all three axes. This is a content ruling as much as a test fix, so it wants the owner's judgement.

title: An item quest grant is recorded unspent by design, so the quest route stays undeclared and 3076 items remain honestly unobtainable

title: One agent mid-writing tools/data.py takes down every tools subcommand for every agent
source:
Measured 2026-10-03 during the acquisition-route and event-validator work. tools/data.py
was observed at 2314 lines mid-write and the loader reported an unterminated string
literal at line 889 while the file at that instant held different text on that line,
which is the signature of a torn read rather than a real syntax error.
next:
Every "uv run python -m tools" subcommand died while one agent was mid-write on
tools/data.py, because data.py is imported by the loader each subcommand uses. One
agent's single edit took fmt, lint, arch, data audit and test down at once for every
concurrent agent. The reported line number pointed at a region that did not match the
file's real content at the same instant - the loader read a torn snapshot - and a
direct ast.parse of the same path succeeded minutes later with no edit in between.
Treat "every tools command is unavailable" as transient and re-verify the file parses
before reporting it as a defect. A structural fix would move the route table into its
own module so the loader's import graph is smaller, but that is a refactor with its
own risk and is not owed while agents are in flight.

title: A single mid-write file in tools/ takes the whole toolchain down, so a gate reading red during concurrent edits is not evidence of a defect
source: Measured 2026-10-03. tools/data.py was 45 lines mid-edit and tools/__main__ refused to load: 'unterminated string literal (line 889) ... every tools command is unavailable until it loads.' That killed fmt --check, lint, arch, data audit and every tracker write at once, while the SAME file parsed cleanly under a direct ast.parse microseconds later (the loader had read a stale snapshot). Two distinct false reds in one hour, both from reading a moving target: (1) tools test printing '433 passed, 0 failed' and exiting 1, which was a file written one second earlier plus, in a second instance, godot.lock contention from my own overlapping runs; (2) fmt reporting 6 files to reformat that agents were actively writing.
next: When a gate stage reads red while agents are in flight, check the file's mtime and parse it directly before believing the message. Never fix a moving file: reformatting or repairing it edits another agent's work mid-write. Wait for mtime to stabilise, then re-measure.

title: Deferring to a live agent is only sound when re-measured: a finished owner left the map gate blocked for hours
source:
Measured twice in one session, opposite outcomes. tools/map_assets.py had been
reported as "owned by a live external agent" for hours; checking git status showed
the file COMMITTED and CLEAN with no write for 90 minutes, and its last commit was
db4fc412. The agent had finished and left, so the deferral was protecting nothing.
Conversely game/src/modules/combat_engine/body_wounds.gd was genuinely dirty and
written 45 seconds before the same check. The two states look identical from the
conversation and only the filesystem distinguishes them.
next:
Never report a file as owned by a live agent from memory or from an earlier
measurement: re-check `git status --short -- <path>` and its mtime before deferring,
and say so with the timestamp. A deferral with no timestamp is indistinguishable from
a real blocker and silently stalls the gate. After fixing a file yourself, verify
which of the OTHER findings are genuinely live the same way rather than assuming the
first sample generalises.

title: The body ascent defect was the missing progress ROW, not missing wording: the unmet list always stated the gate
source:
The orchestrator reported the defect as "the player is owed an ascent and the screen
says nothing about it" and "renders no ascent wording". BOTH were overstated, and the
second body-ascent agent repeated them. Measured against the before-state: unmet[]
already carried "Walk the ascent: 4 of 4 steps to walk", so the player WAS told a gate
existed. What was missing was the ascent ROW - the progress bar and the "4/4" position.
The player was told a gate existed with no indication of how far along the walk they
were. Separately, the claim that the finished-walk branch was also dead is false:
outstanding == "" requires a completed AscensionState, which makes ascension_ok true,
which makes required false, so that branch never matched the first required test - its
assertion was PASSING AT BASELINE. Only the owed case was dead.
next:
Describe a rendering defect by what the node actually contained, not by what the screen
"failed to say". Read the before-drive output verbatim: unmet[] is rendered text too.
When reporting a dead branch, check whether the predicate can reach it before calling it
unreachable - a branch whose assertion passes at baseline was never the defect.

title: The body ascent defect was a missing ROW, not a missing requirement: the sentence was already on screen inside unmet
source:
I briefed both body-ascent agents that "the player is owed an ascent and the screen says
nothing about it". That was false. The before-drive already carried "Walk the ascent: 4 of
4 steps to walk" inside the `unmet` list: the requirement sentence WAS on screen. What was
missing was the ascent ROW - the bar and the player's position in the walk. A player was told
a gate existed, with no progress toward it and nothing stating how far they had come. The
correct defect statement is "no row", not "no wording", and the fix is keyed on `outstanding`
alone so the row can exist.
next:
When briefing a defect from a summary, verify the rendered node AND the read model before
stating what is missing; a populated field and a blank node are different defects with
different fixes. This agent measured it and corrected two of my claims: the `""` branch was
reachable (a completed AscensionState makes required false, so the test never matched) and its
assertion passed at baseline - only the owed case was dead.

title: At the terminal realm an unwalked ascent states a requirement beside a button that is never offered
source:
At the terminal realm an ascent that has not been walked yields required == false while
outstanding is still non-empty, so the screen states a live requirement beside a control
that is not offered. Reached through normal play only if reaching R30 stops requiring
is_complete(); currently unreachable because R30 requires it, and reachable only through
a doctored save. The two halves disagree in body_cultivation/api.gd's required and in
core's ascension_ok terminal exemption, so neither could be fixed from the ui/ files that
owned the row. This is the same "requirement with no affordance" shape that 39b148ef
raised for the NO_ASCENT case.
next:
Decide which of the two owns the terminal exemption: if the walk is genuinely owed at the
terminal realm, ascension_ok must keep required true; if it is genuinely waived, the row
must stop stating it. The split is deliberate in neither place, so one of them is wrong.
Reachable-by-doctored-save does not mean unreachable, and a save editor is not the threat
model here - a player who completes the ladder by an unintended route is.

title: The acquisition count fell 4132 to 1553 because HEAD counted every craft-only item as a delivered root, not because craft stopped working

Cause, measured by loading HEAD and the working tree side by side: HEAD _runtime_roots does 'if kind == craft: continue', which leaves source_type None, so an item whose ONLY source is craft: lands in roots outright and its recipe never has to close. 2791 craft-only items were counted that way and only 216 are reachable through the recipe closure; the other ~2575 rest on inputs no shipping route delivers. HEAD also contradicted its own _obtainable, which deliberately excludes craft from root_types. Roots 4087 vs 1296, reachable 4132 vs 1553. tools/data.py is being edited concurrently (sha changed twice inside one 60s poll), so this fix is uncommitted in-flight work by another agent.
next: When a measurement moves, diff the two implementations rather than reasoning about the delta: importing HEAD and the working tree in one process and comparing roots/reachable named the craft branch in a single run. Never commit a file another agent is actively writing - hash it twice 10s apart first.

title: A Variant-inference parse error in modules/nation/api.gd takes down the whole gate, tools boot included

title: A git index.lock held by live agents blocks commits indefinitely, and removing it corrupts their work rather than unblocking mine
source: Measured 2026-10-03. Six to seven live git processes were committing continuously; the lock reappeared within 60 s of clearing. Two commit attempts failed with 'Unable to create index.lock'. A blanket instruction to 'remove the lock if git crashed' is the standard advice and it is WRONG here: with ~20 concurrent agents, a lock that reappears in under a minute belongs to a live process, and deleting it lets two git processes write one index. HEAD was visibly advancing between attempts (7d5601cc, ba53b3b0, d691e874, 821f71a6).
next: Never remove .git/index.lock in this repo. Check for live git processes and whether HEAD is moving; if so, wait and retry, and leave the work uncommitted rather than force it - uncommitted is recoverable by the next committer, a corrupted index is not. Commit opportunistically between bursts rather than retrying in a loop.

title: A shipped quest step watches a fact no module produces: sect_post_held is the one of five watched ids with no destiny COUNTER_FACTS row, so it reaches the counter side by luck rather than by wiring
source: First measured 2026-10-03 via tools gate_reach check, after the census was taught the roster shape, and it reported 10 quest steps across 5 quests naming a fact no authored beat produced. BOTH halves of that evidence have since rotted and the entry is corrected here rather than deleted; the FINDING under it survives. (1) The `DestinyApi.record` claim is dead: it said 'destiny_projection.gd:152 is the only thing calling DestinyApi.record, and rg finds that call from tests only ... from no production file'. Measured 2026-10-05, that call is at destiny_projection.gd:246 and it IS reached in production, not from a test: `app/item_workbench_app.gd` calls `DestinyProjection.subscribe_to_fact_ledger()` during the composition root's boot, which installs a WorldFact subscriber whose body is `on_fact_recorded`, which reaches `DestinyApi.record` for every fact any of the eight WorldFact writers records. ADR 0148/0149 installed exactly that hook; before it, the claim was true. (2) The count is wrong: the shipped quest tree at game/data/quest/quests watches FIVE distinct facts across 18 fact-gated steps, not ten, and all five have a live producer in game/src - sect_post_held (sect_facts.gd:42), duels_won (combat_facts.gd:31), third_man_spared (combat_facts.gd:34), oaths_discharged (sect_facts.gd:53), household_heir_registered (clan_facts.gd:29). The ten also named the_road_severed, emberblood_furnace_lit, vigil_broken, bound_name_called and mountain_circled_once, and no shipped quest step watches any of those five. (3) What is actually true now, and is the surviving finding: only FOUR of the five watched ids have a COUNTER_FACTS row in destiny_projection.gd, so sect_post_held is written to the world-fact ledger and reaches no fate counter at all. It survives only because COUNTER_FACTS is almost total, not because anything wired it. And the gap is about OTHER MODULES' CONTENT, not about destiny: quest does not choose what a fact is, and destiny does not choose what a module produces. Underneath, the thing that is true and still unactioned is that a `.tres` author writing `fact = &"anything"` in a quest step gets no error, no warning and no red test; the only census over it, tools gate_reach, was reading the WRONG ten ids, so it was reporting the shape of this defect without naming a single fact that is really affected.
next: The decision is unchanged and still one decision; only the evidence above was stale. Either (a) quest steps read the DESTINY ledger through destiny_projection, which needs quest to depend on destiny in registry.json plus a projection that actually satisfies a step - note that today a quest step cannot be satisfied by a COUNTER at all, only by a world fact, so option (a) would need the reader taught to reach the second ledger; or (b) the world_facts ledger is the single ledger and every watched fact keeps a real producer in the module whose action earns it, which is the path already taken for all five watched ids and the one ADR 0114 and the WorldFact writer set assume. Under (b) the remaining gap is the missing COUNTER_FACTS row for sect_post_held - one explicit row, not a derivation - or a decision that the post is a fact no fate should read, which is defensible and should be written down rather than left to look like an oversight. Either way gate_reach must be taught to read the SHIPPED quest tree in the SAME change, and BL-0600's own evidence is the argument for it: a census that asserted ten dead facts when five were live is worse than no census, because it sends an agent to author producers that already exist.

title: Three test_ui_conventions guards assert only inside a filtered loop, so they enforce nothing when nothing matches -- including the ui/ may-not-reach-past-a-facade rule
source: measured 2026-10-03: all three report 'asserted nothing'; game/src/ui holds 52 .gd and 46 .tscn so UI_ROOT and the walker are fine; the shape is the cause. Includes the ui/ facade isolation guard
next: THREE UI GUARD TESTS ARE VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, and one of them is the guard that keeps ui/ from reaching past a module facade. Measured 2026-10-03 on game/tests/ui/test_ui_conventions.gd, which reports `asserted nothing` for all three. MECHANISM: each puts its assert_eq INSIDE a filtered loop, so when nothing matches the filter the body never runs and the test makes ZERO assertions. game/src/ui is not empty -- 52 .gd and 46 .tscn files -- and UI_ROOT is `res://src/ui` (line 17) with a correct recursive walker at :431-451, so this is not a broken path. It is the shape. The three: (1) test_no_ui_file_reaches_a_module_by_anything_but_its_facade at :197 asserts only inside `for module_dir in _module_dirs()` and only for .tscn files, so it says nothing unless some scene instances a module file directly -- and that is EXACTLY the rule that keeps a module's internals out of the UI, so a green run of it proves less than it appears to. (2) test_no_ui_script_uses_onready at :255 asserts per .gd file and should therefore assert ~52 times, so its zero count needs explaining before anyone trusts it; the loop shape alone does not account for it and the real cause is still open. (3) test_ui_scripts_resolve_their_nodes_lazily at :273 skips any file that does not call get_node_or_null, so it is silent on every panel that resolves nothing. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A RED TEST: the test framework reports zero assertions as a FAILURE, which is the right call and stops the rot from being silent -- but the same shape means these guards would have passed unnoticed while enforcing nothing, which is the failure mode test_arch_rules.gd just had (its app/ stateful-system check went quiet because the offender was correctly deleted) and the mode test_no_stranded_mutation.gd addresses by self-hosting a liveness case. NONE OF THIS IS MIND WORK and none of it was touched here. NOT FIXED HERE ON PURPOSE: game/tests/ui is not owned by this session and the file is large and shared. THE FIX IS A LIVENESS TERM, NOT A LOOP CHANGE: each of the three needs a case that asserts unconditionally on a synthetic fixture, the way test_arch_rules.gd's rewrite now asserts that app/ ships a stateful system so its correspondence check cannot pass vacuously, and the way test_no_stranded_mutation.gd holds test_the_guard_does_not_flag_its_own_source. A guard whose only assertions live inside a filter is a guard that can be switched off by the absence of the thing it watches. NEXT: the owner of game/tests/ui adds one unconditional assertion per guard -- for (1) a synthetic scene that DOES instance a module file and must be rejected, for (2) a synthetic script containing @onready that must be caught, for (3) a synthetic panel that resolves nodes without _bind_nodes() -- and each is proved load-bearing by mutation. Until then treat the ui/ facade isolation rule as unguarded.

title: CONFIRMED: the entry band pays a starting hero wearable gear on 2.25% of rolled entries; the grade gate refuses 1078 of the 1254 it does pay
source: root 2026-10-03, boot probe equip phase, with a positive control proving the equip seam itself works
next:
THE SHARPER DEFECT, and it changes the fix. The identical grade mix across bands is not a grading mistake - it is that THE TIER INDEX DOES NOT SELECT DIFFERENT LOOT. Measured directly from the authored encounters rather than inferred from the grade totals:

    tier 1: 329 distinct table ids
    tier 2: 329 distinct table ids
    tier 3: 2      tier 4: 2

    tier 1 vs tier 2: shared 326, only-in-1 3, only-in-2 3   Jaccard 98.2 percent

326 of the 329 tables bound at tier 1 are THE SAME FILES bound at tier 2. So 159 of 160 domains pay an identical loot table at both tiers, and the tier index selects a vitality and a label and nothing else. Only ONE domain in the entire corpus - the ember one, 3 tables: loot_ember_hound/pilgrim/warden at _t1 and _t2 - authored distinct loot per tier. That is why the grade mixes matched to within two items: they are not two similar distributions, they are largely one distribution counted twice.

This supersedes the earlier framing. It is not "grades were authored without regard to band", which implied re-grading items. It is "the deeper band was never authored", which implies writing the tier-2 tables. Those are very different amounts of work and the second is smaller and better specified, because the naming convention and the example both already exist.

THE ONE AUTHORED EXAMPLE DOES NOT ASCEND, which is worth knowing before anyone treats it as the template. loot_ember_warden_t1 stocks greaves_gale at grade=heaven, powder_tide_dust at heaven, D2_heaven_daoheart_sigil at heaven and W5_heaven_ashlar_gossan at heaven. loot_ember_warden_t2 stocks greaves_gale_essence at grade=earth, U23_earth_bracken_aged at earth and bow_yew_wood at mortal. The deeper band pays LOWER grades than the shallower one. Stated as an example and not a trend, because n is 3 tables - too thin to conclude the generator inverts, and far too thin to build a policy on. What it does establish is that this domain is not a working template for depth either; it is the only place per-tier loot exists, and it does not ascend.

WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY IS, stated so it can be estimated. Write per-tier tables for the 159 domains that reuse one table across two tiers, following an authoring rule that grades rise with tier - which means choosing the grade, since grade is a property of the item and cannot be set on the table. The cheapest honest form is to give each tier its own table of the same item ids filtered by a grade window appropriate to the tier, so a tier-2 table cannot pay what a tier-1 table pays. That is mechanical and checkable, and it makes the property testable: a gate asserting that no table is bound at two tiers with the same grade distribution, which is exactly the assertion that would have caught this and which nothing currently asserts.

GATED ON: game/data/loot/ is content and is not claimed by this session, and authoring 159 domains of loot is a balance decision at the scale of the whole game. The measurement is what this entry adds - previously the finding was a symptom (a low gear rate) and now it is a cause (bands share their tables), with the fix specified and the missing assertion named.

title: sect_facts is 4 red and serve() has zero independent coverage, so the failure cannot yet be attributed to the fixture or the implementation
source: Measured 2026-10-03. uv run python -m tools test --suite sect_facts: 41 passed, 4 failed, all in the two oaths_discharged cases. Failure signature, in order: 'a period of service landed: expected true, got false', then 'and the line still owes what it did not clear: expected 2, got 3', then 'the third period cleared the line: expected 1, got 0', then 'and three payments of one period are ONE oath discharged, not three: expected 1, got 0'. owe reporting 3 rather than 2 means serve returned at sect_duty.gd:93 (claim.settled()) BEFORE the settle at :105, so InstitutionClaim.settled() was true - i.e. the claim carried no positive obligation line. Everything downstream is consistent with the fixture's obligation lines vanishing before serve reads them, not with serve mis-settling: SectState.normalize DROPS a line at sect_state.gd:325 (if owed > 0), so the test's strategy of clearing every line but one by writing 0 (test_sect_facts.gd:262-263) and then calling SectApi.attach (line 265) removes exactly the lines it meant to clear, and possibly the one it meant to keep. SectState.MODULE_KEY is &sect_state and api.gd:83 aliases it, so the module key is not the disconnect. What is NOT established, and is the reason this is filed rather than fixed: SectDuty.serve has NO other caller in game/tests - rg finds it only in this one new file - so there is no independent coverage against which to tell a wrong fixture from a wrong implementation, and 'fixing' serve to satisfy a test with no other witness risks replacing correct code.
next: Establish which side is wrong before changing either. Cheapest discriminator: assert inside the test, before serve, that SectState.claim(actor.get_module_data(SectState.MODULE_KEY)).obligation holds exactly the one line the case intends - if it is empty the fixture is wrong, and the fix is to set the fixture AFTER attach or to stop clearing by writing 0, since normalize treats 0 as absent. If it does hold the line, serve is wrong and the early return at sect_duty.gd:93 is the bug. Whoever picks this up should also add a second, independent serve test: a verb with one red test and no other caller is indistinguishable from a verb that works, which is the proof-gap shape BL-0123 was about.

title: dual_cultivation and fertility form a genuine module dependency cycle, which the layer rules forbid outright
source: Measured 2026-10-03 with tools arch: 'module dependency cycle: dual_cultivation -> fertility -> dual_cultivation'. Both modules are being actively written (newest files 7 and 19 minutes old), so this is in-flight work by a live agent and is recorded rather than fixed. The cycle is real code, not prose: dual_cultivation/seduction.gd:45 does const FERTILITY_FACADE := preload(res://src/modules/fertility/api.gd) and then calls can_conceive twice, try_conceive once and conception_chance once (lines 47, 50, 71, 76 by the call sites found). The reverse edge is thinner and materially different in kind: fertility/provider.gd:9 reads context.value(DualCultivationApi.FERTILITY) and fertility/api.gd:85 reads partner.stats.get_base(DualCultivationApi.POTENCY) - two STAT ID CONSTANTS, with no call into a dual-cultivation verb.
next: The two edges are not the same kind of dependency and the fix should not treat them as symmetric. One direction is behaviour (dual_cultivation drives conception), the other is vocabulary (fertility needs to name two stats). Options, best first: (1) move FERTILITY and POTENCY as stat ids into contracts/ or core/, where a shared vocabulary belongs, and have both modules read them from there - this dissolves the reverse edge outright and is almost certainly the right answer, since a stat id is a contract and not a dependency; (2) if the stat ids must stay module-owned, fertility must not name them at all and the projection moves to whoever owns both, which is app/. Do NOT solve this with a preload in either direction - that is what already produced the cycle. Needs an ADR: it moves stat vocabulary across a layer boundary, and per the repository rule a contracts/ or core/ change ships with its ADR in the same change.

title: Domains Storm Phoenix and Storm Hawk: the boss dies and mints no reward at all
source: root 2026-10-04, boot probe sweep of 8 domain/tier pairs in a real boot of the shipped main scene
next: NARROWED TO THE RUNTIME MINT PATH - the entire authored data chain verifies correct, and three plausible data-side explanations are now refuted. CONFIRMED CORRECT (do not re-check these): 160 domains, each claimed by exactly ONE encounter - zero domains are claimed by more than one, so there is no arbitrary-resolution race; each encounter binds exactly the bosses its domain spawns, overlap 2 of 2 on every sampled pair including Storm Phoenix and Storm Hawk; all 336 distinct table ids referenced by encounters resolve to files; the failing tables hold 21, 19 and 19 item entries; zero of the 320 authored tiers have an empty boss_tables. THE TIER REALM - my own hypothesis, and wrong. contextualize takes the tier realm and rarity, so realm looked like the filter, but the PAYING table loot_amulet_iron_sage has 0 of 21 items matching its own tier realm void_refinement while the FAILING loot_amulet_storm_phoenix has 1 of 21 matching spirit_unity. If realm were the filter the paying table would mint nothing too. 2. title: BL-0114 residue: authored content still targets the RETIRED mind stat id dodge_chance, so half of passive_quick_reaction is an inert no-op
source: root 2026-10-04, second BL-0114 wave. Measured, not inferred: rg over game/ finds cult_dodge_chance in exactly 3 files.
next: REPORTED, NOT FIXED - game/data/ and modules/items are not mind_cultivation's to edit, and the fix is a content decision, not a code one. EVIDENCE. game/data/item_options/master_option_pool.jsonl:42 declares cult_dodge_chance with status active, family mind, op PERCENT, unit rate, weight 5.0 and target {type: stat, id: dodge_chance}. game/data/techniques/passive_quick_reaction.tres:20 ships it as {option_id: cult_dodge_chance, value: 5.0} and its description promises 'Dodge chance and mental attack'. game/data/item_options/derived/option_pools.json lists it in 5 entries (lines 97, 269, 345, 421, 446), so equipment can also roll it. WHY IT IS INERT: MindProvider.contribute emits exactly the 7 ids pinned by test_mind_stat_surface.gd:34-42 and dodge_chance is not among them; core's own id is Stat.EVASION = evasion (contracts/stat.gd:42), so the string matches NEITHER module. OptionCatalog.make_effect (option_catalog.gd:308-318) therefore normalises it to target_id = dodge_chance, and ActorStats._ensure_providers (actor_stats.gd:116-125) only ever applies a PERCENT modifier to a bucket a provider actually fills, so the +5.0 is multiplied against nothing. SCOPE: 1 technique (half its effects) + up to 5 pools. critical_chance has NO residue - zero references to it anywhere in game/. THE DECISION FOR THE OWNER, and it is genuinely two ways: (a) retarget the option to mind_avoidance, which makes the technique's promise true but spends a stat that is ADR 0071's MindDamage coherence roll, so it is a mind-duellist buff and the label 'Dodge Chance' must change too; or (b) retire the option, which leaves a common-grade pool entry and a shipped technique needing replacement. title: ADR 0071 required a save migration note for the critical_chance/dodge_chance rename and none was ever written, so an old save silently loses both stats
source: root 2026-10-04, second BL-0114 wave. ADR 0071 Consequences, line 48, states the obligation: 'The two renamed ids are a save-affecting rename: critical_chance/dodge_chance need a migration note alongside the schema history.' Measured: rg for critical_chance, dodge_chance, mind_focus_chance, mind_avoidance and cult_dodge across game/src/modules/save/ and game/src/core/actor.gd returns NOTHING. SaveMigrate exists (referenced from modules/save/save_slot.gd) but no step of it mentions either old or new id.
next: REPORTED, NOT FIXED - modules/save and core/actor.gd are not this wave's to edit, and the correct fix is a save-module decision. WHY IT MATTERS: the rename changed two stat ids an actor payload can carry. core/actor.gd owns the actor payload's version and modules/save/save_slot.gd:17 records that SCHEMA_VERSION is pinned and must not be bumped for a new world key, so the question is whether this rename bumped the ACTOR payload version at all and, if it did not, what a pre-rename save does with a payload naming critical_chance/dodge_chance - drop them silently, or round-trip them as unknown keys. Either way the player who cultivated before the rename has silently weaker mind damage. WHAT TO DECIDE: (a) add a SaveMigrate step rewriting the two old ids to mind_focus_chance/mind_avoidance, which is the faithful reading of ADR 0071 line 48; or (b) declare the pre-rename payload unsupported and bump the actor version so old saves are refused rather than half-read, and amend ADR 0071's consequence because it asked for a migration note and not a refusal. RELATED, and the same shape: BL-0636 records authored content still TARGETING the retired dodge_chance, so the rename was applied in res://src and missed in game/data/ and in save. THREE PLACES, ONE RENAME - worth checking all three the next time an id changes, because the guard that caught the src side (test_mind_renamed_stat_ids.gd) cannot see either of the other two.

title: mutation_history flags probes on refs/remotes/origin/* that are the same in-flight work already flagged locally, doubling one finding
source: Measured 2026-10-04 while an agent was mid-mutation-prove in mind_cultivation. The guard reported four findings: two on refs/remotes/origin/HEAD and two on refs/remotes/origin/main, all naming MUTATION markers that are ALSO live in the local working tree (provider.gd:47 MUTATION-B, training.gd:255 MUTATION-ANCHOR-1, and three in test_mind_stat_reachability.gd). Local main is 3 commits ahead of origin/main with 0 behind, so origin/main is a STALE copy of work that has since moved - it is not a shipped ref in the sense the guard means. One broken implementation therefore reports as several findings, which trains an agent to read the count as severity and discount the guard.
next: Decide whether refs/remotes/* belongs in SHIPPED_REFS at all. The argument for keeping it: a probe pushed to a remote and never fixed is still in everyone's clone, and a guard that only reads the local branch would call a repository clean while origin/main is broken. The argument for dropping it: a remote-tracking ref here is a stale mirror of local work in a repo nobody pushes to deliberately, so it double-reports in-flight mutations and makes the gate noisier than the hazard. The honest fix is probably to keep refs/remotes/* but deduplicate by CONTENT rather than by ref - report one finding per distinct (path, marker) with the refs that carry it, so one broken file is one finding however many refs hold it. Either way, do not let the count grow silently.

title: UNFIXABLE HERE: no shipped verb restores an Actor's providers, so every module's whole stat surface is lost on load unless the caller re-runs that module's attach by hand
source: measured 2026-10-04 while fixing BL-0108. Actor.from_dict (core/actor.gd:343) restores identity, resources, paths, meridians, components, module_data and every versioned slot, and installs NO StatProvider: an Actor.new() starts with ActorStats._providers empty and nothing in from_dict appends to it. There is no shipped 'restore and re-attach' verb either - PlayerAdapter.from_dict (app/player_adapter.gd:287) is the only from_dict caller in src and nothing calls IT, and ActorFactory.build (which is where the shared providers are mounted) is not reachable from from_dict. So restoration is currently 'whoever loads must remember to call attach again, per module', and forgetting one is silent: no error, the stats simply read absent. BL-0108 was exactly one instance of this - MindCultivationApi.attach_sea returned the component it found before registering SeaProvider, so a restored actor had a sea and no published surface, and MindStats.SEA_CAPACITY vanished from ActorStats.derived_all() so the 'Sea capacity' row disappeared from the routed CharacterScreen with nothing logged. Fixed inside the mind facade because that is the only file its owner had; the class of defect is not mind's.
next: One verb in app/ (the composition root, which is already the only layer that knows concrete provider types) that takes an Actor.from_dict result and runs the whole attach spine: ActorFactory.build's four providers plus every module attach the actor's paths imply, mirroring with_mind_cultivation / with_qi_cultivation / with_body_cultivation. Then make PlayerAdapter.from_dict call it, so there is exactly one load path and a forgotten module is impossible rather than silent. Needs an ADR: it is app/ wiring over core's restore boundary and changes what a load is allowed to do. Until then, a cheap guard is possible per module - a test that round-trips through the shipped to_dict/from_dict, re-attaches only as production does, and asserts the provider count is unchanged, which is the shape of game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_sea_provider_round_trip.gd.

title: test_screen_reachability's SUFFIXES table can never match get_extension(), so the BL-0121 door check scans nothing and reports a false positive
source: Measured 2026-10-04, same defect class as BL-0622. test_screen_reachability.gd:25 declares SUFFIXES as a dotted list ([".gd", ".tscn"]) and line 439 is its only use: SUFFIXES.has(entry.get_extension()). String.get_extension() returns the extension WITHOUT the dot ("gd"), so the membership test is false for every file and _source_texts() returns an empty list for every root. Proven by the sibling fix, not assumed: in test_ui_conventions.gd the identical dotted filter on .gd/.tscn skipped all 53 scripts under res://src/ui and the guard reported "asserted nothing"; changing it to the dot-free form took that same scan from 0 to 53 assertions. Consequence measured: uv run python -m tools test --suite app/test_screen_reachability gives Results: 362 passed, 1 failed, failing on "res://src/app/item_workbench_app.gd is public and opens a screen, but nothing in src/ or scenes/ calls open_creation(); it is a route only a test can use (BL-0121)". That is FALSE of the tree: game/src/app/item_workbench_app.gd:162 calls open_creation(). THIS CORRECTS BL-0647, which predicted the failure would go green by itself once the peer committed the production caller. The caller is in the tree and the guard still reports zero callers, because it never read a single file.
next: One token: make SUFFIXES dot-free at test_screen_reachability.gd:25. Both occurrences are in that one file, which is committed and clean, so nobody has it in flight. NOT FIXED HERE because it is not my file. Then re-run --suite app/test_screen_reachability and expect 363 passed / 0 failed. Do NOT make the failure go away by editing item_workbench_app.gd: the caller is already there and is correct. While fixing it, follow BL-0622: a scan that can read nothing must assert that it read something, or the next person re-breaks it silently.

title: UNWIRED: the AWARENESS reserve has no writer, so ADR 0071's coherence term and both chance terms are constant zero and erosion Kind ATTEND drains nothing
source: MEASURED 2026-10-04, not a reading of the backlog. Nothing in res://src ever WRITES the awareness pool: rg for awareness across game/src returns only MindStats.AWARENESS (stats.gd:55), the pool CREATION at mind_cultivation/api.gd:209-210 (_add_pool with full=false, so current stays 0.0 against a 100.0 maximum), and reads. The three consequences, all verified by test_mind_stat_reachability.gd rather than asserted: (1) provider.gd:61-62 publish mind_focus_chance and mind_avoidance with awareness_ratio*0.1 and *0.05, so both are constant 0.05+perception*0.003 and perception*0.002 - the dial ADR 0071's FOCUS_MULT and COHERENCE_DAMP are spent on is fixed; (2) mind_damage.gd:233/532 computes coherence = 1 - coherence_damp*0.0 = 1.0 ALWAYS, so the shipped coherence_damp=0.5 (combat_damage.tres:23) never halves anything and ADR 0071's '1.0 -> 0.5 at full awareness' is unreachable; (3) mind_damage.gd:586-588 awareness_delta is -clampf(0.0*erosion) = 0.0, so erosion Kind.ATTEND (mind_damage.gd:102, 'drains the AWARENESS reserve') drains nothing. Consequence for a player: ADR 0071:35 names awareness as defensive lever (1) of four, and the cheapest one to hold. Today it cannot be held at all. NOTE the dead local BL-0154 named is NOT this: mind_power_ratio is gone (provider.gd:29-40), and the six other published ids ARE read - see the BL-0154 disposition.
next: NOT FIXABLE by editing provider.gd, which is why it is filed rather than repaired. The writer belongs to training.gd (owned elsewhere) and WHAT funds awareness is an unanswered design question, not a code change: ADR 0013:13 calls it 'perceptual acuity, affects detection/crit/dodge' (a permanent reserve you refill) while ADR 0071:35 calls it 'the DEPLETING AWARENESS reserve' (a resource spent to blunt a strike). Those are different verbs - refill vs spend - and reconciling them needs its own ADR before any verb is written. Options for that ruling: cultivation work funds it (a rate on MindTraining.cultivate, the one action that already funds clarity/purity/progress), or a technique spends it, or awareness is deleted and coherence drops out of the formula. Whichever is chosen, MindDamage already reads and drains it correctly, so the wiring exists and only the writer is missing. test_mind_stat_reachability.gd test_the_awareness_terms_are_inert_and_that_is_pinned asserts the inertness today, so it goes RED the moment a writer appears - that is the signal to re-check ADR 0071's 1.0->0.5 claim rather than a silent success.

title: 35 public facade verbs ship with no test reference, including the whole of ForageApi
source: Found by generalising the BL-0123 proof gap I committed myself: ADR 0145 shipped serve_duty with no test, and MUTATION-S1 proved deleting it left modules/sect at 1393 passed / 0 failed. So I scanned for the class rather than the instance. Counted with a deliberately narrow rule after the first attempt returned a useless 1250 - most of those are _private helpers, and a private helper is SUPPOSED to be reached through the public verb that calls it, so counting it untested is backwards. The useful population is PUBLIC static verbs on a modules/*/api.gd facade, which is the only surface other modules and ui/ may call: 35 have no test reference at all, attach excluded. Named ones include AnchorApi.cost_of/pay_down/shelters/state/summary (all five), BloodlineApi.bloodline_ids, BodyCultivationApi.meditate/strengthen_next, CombatApi.player/resolve_share/offense/guard, CombatEngineApi.resolve_hit/summary, EconomyApi.quote, ElementsApi.multiplier/strip_realm_modifiers, four FertilityApi verbs, HoldingsApi.validate, and both ForageApi verbs - so the forager module that the acquisition audit said could not exist now EXISTS and is itself untested.
next: Triage in two piles rather than writing 35 tests. Pile one is verbs that are dead: no test AND no production caller, which is the SectDuty.serve shape a commit ago and means the feature does not exist however much prose it carries - ForageApi is the prime suspect given nothing routes to gathering. Pile two is verbs that are live but unobserved: called from app/ or ui/, no test, so a change to them is invisible and they are one mutation from being wrong. Measure which pile each falls in before writing anything; a verb that is both dead and untested needs a decision (wire it or delete it), not a test. Note that tests/arch_rules/test_fact_ledger_writers.gd already pins the WRITER set, so this asks the different and unanswered question of whether a verb is exercised at all.

title: guardian_vigil_ash declares a boss source no boss grants, and data audit correctly fails on it
source: Measured 2026-10-04. uv run python -m tools data audit fails with 'item guardian_vigil_ash: source boss has no reference', and it is the ONLY such finding in the corpus - so this is one item's data rather than a class. The item is game/data/items/consumable/guardian_vigil_ash.tres:20, sources = [&boss, &domain:qi_spirit_ascension_trial]. The domain half is real and delivers: game/data/domains/qi_spirit_ascension_trial.tres exists, game/data/loot/encounters/loot_qi_spirit_ascension_trial.tres grants it, and game/data/bosses/F12_ascension_warden.tres exists. So the item IS obtainable and the boss entry alone is the dangling half. rg over game/data finds the id in exactly one file - the item itself - so no boss, loot table or domain names it. The file was written at 03:09 today and is plausibly an in-flight agent's, so recorded rather than edited.
next: One of two honest fixes, and the choice belongs to whoever authored the item. Either drop the &boss entry, leaving the real domain route and taking data audit green immediately; or keep it and make it true by adding guardian_vigil_ash to a boss's drop set - F12_ascension_warden is the obvious candidate given the domain pairing, and the acquisition guard would then verify the delivery rather than trusting the label. What must NOT happen is adding an --ignore or relaxing the validator: the finding is correct, and the acquisition agent already proved this exact guard catches a source that names nothing. A boss source that grants nothing is the ADR 0066 quiet lie in one field.

title: selftest is red on a lore guard: --force does not discard the hand-written summary, so the destructive flag is wired to nothing
source: Observed 2026-10-04 while tools/lore was being actively written (model.py at 05:01, ingest.py at 04:57, now 05:08), so this is a live agent's in-flight state and is recorded rather than fixed. The failing case is 'lore: --force IS destructive, and says so', and its own message is the finding: '--force did not discard the hand-written summary, so the flag that warns about data loss is wired to nothing and the safe default is the only reachable path'. Note the run also printed a warn that --force discarded agent-authored summary/tags/name on every imported record - so the two observations disagree, which is worth the agent's attention rather than mine: either the discard is unconditional (and the test is right that the flag is decorative) or the test fixture is not reaching the discard path at all.
next: Whichever way it resolves, the shape is the one this repo keeps meeting: a flag that exists, is documented as destructive, and changes nothing is worse than no flag, because an agent reading the help text will believe their hand-written prose is disposable. The guard is doing its job by being red - do not quieten it. Whoever owns tools/lore should make --force actually force, or remove it, and the self-test then pins whichever was chosen.

title: UNWIRED, last of four: MindRealmSeed.insight_required is exactly 0.5x comprehension_required at all 30 realms and is read by nothing
source: Measured 2026-10-04, not inferred. insight_required == 0.5 * comprehension_required at 30/30 realms (mismatch count 0). comprehension_required is the ENFORCED gate on the same stat at breakthrough_condition.gd:27 and advancement.gd:81,165, so a strictly weaker copy of a threshold that already binds can never be the deciding term. Grep finds one reader in the whole tree and it is a TEST: game/tests/modules/test_seed_generator_parity.gd:304 (test_mind_insight_is_half_of_comprehension). Nothing in res://src, tools/ or docs/adr/ reads it. Deleting it was mutation-proven to cost EXACTLY that one case and nothing else: removing all four @exports with the 30 .tres untouched gave 15532 passed / 0 failed on --suite mind_cultivation and 691 passed / 1 failed on --suite seed_generator_parity, the single red being 'SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid access to property or key insight_required on a base object of type Resource (MindRealmSeed)'. Not a compile error, so the blast radius is one case. Also measured: a .tres line for a property the class dropped is SILENTLY IGNORED by Godot 4.7 - no error, no warning - so leaving the line costs nothing and only the tools/cultivation/seed_systems.py:227 writer is stale.
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL, and the numbers are confirmed rather than inherited: I recomputed the identity off the 30 seeds and got 0 mismatches, so insight_required == comprehension_required * 0.5 at 30/30 realms. Three edits, all recorded here so the next agent does not re-derive them, and the blast radius is one case. (1) Delete the @export var insight_required block from game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/realm_seed.gd:36. (2) Delete test_mind_insight_is_half_of_comprehension from game/tests/modules/test_seed_generator_parity.gd:298-307. (3) Drop the insight_required line from tools/cultivation/seed_systems.py:227 - and note the measured asymmetry that makes (3) safe to do LAST or not at all: Godot 4.7 SILENTLY IGNORES a .tres property the class dropped (no error, no warning), so the 30 .tres need no edit and the generator line costs nothing until a regeneration, which is filed as its own entry rather than folded in here. Then drop insight_required from the deleted-to-add list in game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_mind_seed_unread_fields.gd, whose three legs (class property list, shipped .tres text, unconditional liveness term) are what made this class measurable at all. THE MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, unchanged: removing all four @exports while the 30 seeds still authored them cost test_mind_insight_is_half_of_comprehension and NOTHING else - 15532 passed / 0 failed on --suite mind_cultivation, 691 passed / 1 failed on --suite seed_generator_parity, the single red being 'Invalid access to property or key insight_required on a base object of type Resource (MindRealmSeed)'. Not a compile error, so the deletion cannot cascade. STILL REJECTED AS FAKE WORK, and this is the part worth keeping: do not wire it as a gate. comprehension_required is already ENFORCED on the same stat at breakthrough_condition.gd:27 and advancement.gd:81,165, so a threshold at half that value can never be the deciding term - a gate that cannot bind is not a gate. See ADR 0147:44-48 for the reasoning and docs/adr/0147-the-unread-mindrealmseed-fields-are-deleted-rather-than-wired.md for the disposition of the other three.

title: A mutation probe disabling the technique binding guard is COMMITTED on main; the working tree is fixed but the commit is not
source: Found by uv run python -m tools mutation_history check, the guard built for exactly this (INC-0013). Commit b9dc618a 'add some src' shipped game/src/modules/techniques/technique_delivery.gd with 'if not is_bound() and false:  # MUTATION-M6' - a probe that disables the technique binding guard outright, so main serves unbound techniques. The WORKING TREE is already correct (line 163 reads 'if not is_bound():' with no 'and false'), but that fix is UNCOMMITTED: git diff shows 23 insertions / 10 deletions against HEAD. So HEAD is broken and the tree is not, which is why test_no_stranded_mutation.gd stays green - it reads the working tree, and the probe exists only in history. Verified with git show HEAD:..., which is what makes this a finding rather than a suspicion.
next: Commit the restoration, then confirm mutation_history check goes green for this ref. Do NOT use git restore or git checkout on this path - they take every other agent's uncommitted work with them and have destroyed finished work in this repo twice; the correct repair is to commit the working tree, which already holds the fix. Worth asking separately why a commit named 'add some src' was able to carry a probe at all: the guard that should have caught it reads the tree rather than the ref, so a probe can be committed whenever the tree is clean at commit time - which is precisely the window in which a mutation-prove agent is most likely to be running.

title: RATE_STATS cannot see the mind module's two rate stats, so a FLAT on mind_focus_chance or mind_avoidance passes every guard
source: BL-0636 fix, measured 2026-10-04 while retargeting cult_dodge_chance
next: CONFIRMED BLIND SPOT, NOT FIXED: contracts/ is off-limits to the BL-0636 fix and contracts/ changes need their own ADR. contracts/stat.gd:73-84 declares RATE_STATS = [ATTACK_SPEED, BREAKTHROUGH_CHANCE, COOLDOWN_REDUCTION, CRIT_CHANCE, CRIT_DAMAGE, CULTIVATION_RATE, EVASION, INSIGHT_GAIN, QI_COST_REDUCTION, STATUS_RESISTANCE] and omits mind_focus_chance AND mind_avoidance, both of which are fraction baselines the same shape as the entries it does hold (mind_cultivation/provider.gd:61-62 = minf(0.75, 0.05 + perception*0.003 + awareness_ratio*0.1) and minf(0.6, perception*0.002 + awareness_ratio*0.05)). WHY IT MATTERS: the list exists to reject a FLAT on a rate stat, because core resolves (base + flat) * (1 + percent) (core/actor_stats.gd:192-196) so +10 on a 0..1 stat means 1000 percent. That guard is therefore SILENT about both mind rate ids: an option authored op FLAT on mind_avoidance would validate clean and apply as 5000 percent, not as +10. The guard's silence is not evidence these two ids are correct. THE FIX NEEDS AN ADR because it edits contracts/, and because the list is core-owned: the mind module cannot add its own ids to a core constant. Candidates to weigh: move RATE_STATS to a per-module declaration with core aggregating, or give ActorStats/OptionCatalog one is_rate_stat() that queries each module's published rate set. Note this is a THIRD place the rate/baseline taxonomy is restated after Stat.RATE_STATS and CombatStats.RATE_IDS. NOTE the guard's silence did NOT affect BL-0636: cult_dodge_chance is op PERCENT, the valid case.

BL-0636's next field claims no guard existed and that adding one 'would go RED on this exact line today, so adding it would have meant committing a failing test'. The guard already exists: tools/check.py:82 runs ('data', ['options', 'coverage', '--fail-on', 'error']), described in its own comment as 'every registered option target must have an implemented consumer (ADR 0025/0033)'. Re-planting the retired id (master_option_pool.jsonl target id dodge_chance, catalog sha256 0123a0afeb56258ed047e1d879fd36e9513fb78940fa8604032a411eec15b525) makes that step print 'fail dodge_chance: no implemented consumer (cult_dodge_chance)' and exit non-zero; with the retarget it prints 'ok option coverage: 104/104 targets have an implemented consumer'. So tools check was FAILING on this defect before it was fixed, and BL-0636's own measurement missed a step that was already red. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) When a content defect is reported as invisible, run the gates before believing it: this class was detectable in about a second. (2) The coverage gate proves a CONSUMER EXISTS, not that a modifier HAS AN EFFECT: it classifies a target as core/provider/element/property/resource and mind_avoidance passes as 'provider'. A PERCENT on a stat whose baseline is identically zero would also pass coverage and still be inert, which is exactly the ADR 0022 trap documented at core/actor_stats.gd:181-186 where damage_reduction is deliberately kept out of RATE_STATS for the same reason. That residual gap is now covered in the GDScript suite by game/tests/modules/mind_cultivation/test_mind_option_target_liveness.gd, which asserts a rolled value MOVES the stat by the exact factor the consumption path defines. STILL TRUE AND UNFIXED: BL-0636's scope claim about game/data/techniques/passive_quick_reaction.tres:20 shipping the option at value 5.0 is FALSE on the current tree. That file is 7 lines with no fixed modifiers, and rg over game/ finds cult_dodge_chance only in master_option_pool.jsonl and 5 lines of derived/option_pools.json. BL-0636 was left unrewritten per the never-rewrite rule; this is the correction.

title: An unreachable tribulation refusal is a trap: deleting one neighbouring guard makes nonsense text player-visible
source: Found by the failure-branch audit, and the most interesting of its unreachable rows because it is a trap rather than a harmless guard. tribulation_fight.gd:57 refuses with "the tribulation would not begin", but begin_tribulation only returns null on a sub-threshold index guard which the sole caller has already excluded, so nothing can trigger this branch. title: begin_breakthrough/resolve_breakthrough have zero callers, so an attempt cannot survive a save and the facade's documented two-phase promise is unimplemented
source: Found by the failure-branch audit. BodyCultivationApi.begin_breakthrough / resolve_breakthrough - the documented DURABLE, save-spanning half of the breakthrough lifecycle - have zero callers in res://src (proven by source scan). attempt_breakthrough runs both halves inside a single call, so no state a player can produce has an attempt in flight, panel_state attempt is permanently the empty string, and a save taken mid-attempt is impossible. The facade docstring promises that a panel renders an attempt is committed from it and offers resolve rather than a fresh breakthrough; body_cultivation_panel.gd never reads attempt, so that promise is unimplemented. This is BL-0130 territory - the user decision was to WIRE start_attempt/resolve_attempt through api.attempt_breakthrough matching mind, and the single-call version was satisfied, but the two-phase durable half it replaced is still unwired. The audit proved the machinery WORKS when a caller drives it (test_the_unreachable_durable_half_works_when_a_caller_drives_it), so this is unwired rather than broken.
next: A decision, not a test. Either build the affordance - the panel offers resolve for an attempt already in flight, which is what makes a tribulation or a death mid-breakthrough survivable across a save - or delete the claim from the facade docstring so the next reader does not design against a promise that is not there. Building it is the better product and is squarely on the acceptance gate: a save taken mid-attempt is currently impossible, so a player who quits during an attempt loses it silently. BodyCultivationApi is at the 12-method cap, so check whether this needs a facade method at all before assuming it does - the read model already publishes an attempt field, so a writer may be the only missing piece.

title: summary() reports a not-yet-unlocked channel as injured: true
source: game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/api.gd:100 reads channel.is_injured() if channel != null else true, so all 20 meridians report injured at R1 where only 4 are unlocked; found while making mind_cultivation_screen name the missing elixir (ADR 0151)
next: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-04 (session mind-ledger) - STILL REAL, one line, unchanged: game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/api.gd:100 reads "injured": channel.is_injured() if channel != null else true, so a channel the network has not unlocked yet reports injured: true. At R1 only 4 meridians are unlocked and the other 16 answer true, which is a lie about 16 rows a player can see. WHY IT SURVIVED: every consumer learned to filter. game/src/ui/screens/mind_cultivation_screen.gd:508-510 does String(entry.get("state", "")) != "unknown" and bool(entry.get("injured", false)) - i.e. the screen already knows the answer is unreliable and works around it, with a comment at :495-497 saying exactly that ('yet on the network as injured: true; counting those would answer "you owe an elixir" to a hero who has never been burned'). That workaround is correct and it is also the argument for fixing the source rather than the caller: the filter lives in ui/ because ui/ is the only consumer that noticed. FIX, cheapest first: report injured: false for a channel that is not on the network, since 'not yet unlocked' is not 'hurt' and no consumer wants the conflation. Better: publish the unlocked flag alongside injured - api.gd already publishes state (:97, 'unknown' when absent) and required (:102, the gate this realm applies), so an unlocked key is a third field on a shape that is already carrying per-channel state, and it costs no facade method. EITHER WAY add the assertion: today nothing fails if the 'else true' becomes 'else false' or if a caller drops the state filter, because the screen's workaround makes both readings look the same to the suite. This is a one-line module change with a one-line test; it is open only because nobody has picked it up, not because it is hard.

title: The restored actor's sea COMPONENT round-trips while its sea PROVIDER does not, so a component-shaped assertion cannot see a dropped attach
source: Measured 2026-10-04 while proving the read half. MUTATION-C (drop the mind attach from ActorFactory.restore_cultivation, leaving the other two) ran GREEN at 84 passed / 0 failed: every assertion on sea tier, clarity, capacity, the trained meridian and the resonance rank still held, because Actor.from_dict restores SeaOfConsciousness as a component and nothing in the payload restores a StatProvider. The composition root is the only layer that may install a provider (core may not name modules, and providers are app/'s to wire), so no unit-level guard in core/ or contracts/ can close this; every such assertion has to be a derived_all() membership check at the composition-root seam.

title: Root cause of the 224-pending boot failure: the world drop container holds 6, so pickups overflow and the claim is deliberately not spent
source: root 2026-10-05, read against loot_state.gd while the claim agent works
next: MY OWN CENTRAL CLAIM IN THIS ENTRY IS WRONG. Correcting it before the running agent chases it. WHAT I SAID: that 224 pending is the world-drop container overflowing, so the claim is deliberately not spent and the probe is reporting a real collection as a failure. THAT IS REFUTED BY THE CODE I THEN READ. LootRewards.view at loot_rewards.gd:172-186 counts a drop as claimed, else stashed, else pending - and stashed IS the world-drop container state. So a drop that overflowed into the container is STASHED and is NOT counted as pending. 224 pending therefore means 224 drops that are neither claimed nor stashed: the pickup never marked them at all. This is a genuine collection failure, not a measurement artifact. Do not chase the overflow theory; the code rules it out. THE REAL LEAD, from reading LootState.pickup at loot_state.gd:398. It has four named refusals before it mutates anything, and three of them fit what we see: is_spent returns ERR_CLAIM_SPENT when the whole encounter payload is already spent (401-404); rewards.has(encounter) false returns ERR_UNKNOWN_REWARD (406-412); _drop_index returning -1 for the pressed drop_id returns ERR_UNKNOWN_DROP (419-427). The last is the one to check first, because the reward list is POOLED: a row can outlive the reward it was built for. When claiming a reward retires its payload from state[rewards] and the next reward slides into view, a pooled row whose drop_id belonged to the retired payload yields ERR_UNKNOWN_DROP - a refusal the player cannot act on, and exactly the shape where pending stays flat. THE INSTRUMENTATION THAT SETTLES IT: the refusal REASON is returned by pickup and surfaced by the screen, so one probe run that reports the refusal reason per press distinguishes all four branches at once. Do not infer it from pending alone. STILL OWNED BY THE RUNNING CLAIM AGENT - I changed nothing in modules/loot, and these are read-only observations to save it time.

title: A mutation-marker can sit in the git INDEX and reach history unseen by the stranded-mutation guard
source: INC-0024, observed 2026-10-04 while mutation-proving the loot world-full refusal
next: WHAT HAPPENED. I planted MUTATION-LOOTWORLDFULL in game/src/modules/loot/loot_state.gd to prove a refusal-reason fix load-bearing. While that marker was live, a separate agent recovered from an upstream error and ran git add on that same file. The INDEX therefore held 'reason: ERR_INVENTORY_FULL,  # MUTATION-LOOTWORLDFULL'. Had its commit landed, the marker would be in history permanently. I caught it by reading 'git diff --cached' after noticing the file showed MM (staged AND unstaged) rather than the M I expected from my own edit. Cleared with 'git reset -- <path>' scoped to my one file. THE GAP. test_no_stranded_mutation.gd is a WORKING-TREE guard: it reads files, so it cannot see a marker that lives only in the index or already in a commit. That is the INC-0007 shape (a probe captured into history by another agent's commit) with a second entrance nobody has guarded - the index itself. WHY IT IS WORTH A GUARD RATHER THAN A NOTE. Three things had to coincide: (1) a mutation window, (2) a second agent staging the same path in that window, (3) no guard reading the index. Two of the three are ordinary practice, so the expected value of this is not low. NOTE THE ORDERING TRAP I HIT FIRST, because it is the part a reader will do wrong. My own revert made the working tree correct while the index stayed wrong. 'git diff' showed the fix in place and I nearly concluded the tree was clean; only 'git diff --cached' showed the marker. A fix-forward revert repairs the worktree, never the index. WHAT TO BUILD. A guard that refuses a commit whose INDEX differs from its worktree on any path containing a live marker, i.e. run the same classification mutation_history._live_marker uses over 'git diff --cached' output. Cheaper variant with most of the value: assert the index has no live marker at all, which is true on a healthy tree and is exactly the state that must not be committed. title: Overflow parking is unobservable through the screen: the state IS saved but the view never repaints
source: diagnosed 2026-10-04 from test_loot_overflow.gd:252-254, while verifying the ERR_WORLD_FULL refusal label
next: DIAGNOSED. CORRECTION FIRST, because I asserted the opposite and was wrong. I previously wrote that this is 'the same root cause as the 224-pending measurement in BL-0697'. THAT IS REFUTED by code I have now read. LootEncounterScreen.act_pickup (game/src/ui/screens/loot_encounter.gd:156-166) calls _reward_list.report_outcome(...) then _settle(result), and _settle (:545-546) calls refresh(). So the screen DOES republish on the player's own control path. The boot probe presses a real Button - boot_probe.gd:570 does action.pressed.emit() on the DropAction node - which routes through act_pickup, so the probe's view repaints too. Therefore this defect CANNOT explain 224 pending, and criterion 3 must be diagnosed elsewhere. Do not close BL-0697 on the strength of this fix. THE REAL DEFECT, which stands. A pickup driven through the FACADE (LootApi.pickup, api.gd:156-163) mutates and saves state - _save(actor, state) at :161 - but never reaches the screen, so the rendered view goes stale. test_loot_overflow.gd's _first_pickup (:280-291) does exactly that, then reads listed_reward (:291-292) which returns view.summary(), and gets pre-pickup values. THE SEPARATE LEAD FOR CRITERION 3, which is more likely and belongs to BL-0697. boot_probe.gd:567-570 resolves the first node named DropAction inside the reward list and emits on it. If the reward list is POOLED, that node can be a STALE row whose drop_id belonged to a reward already retired from state[rewards]; LootState.pickup then returns ERR_UNKNOWN_DROP (loot_state.gd:419-427), a refusal the player cannot act on, and pending stays flat. The probe re-resolves the screen each pass but not the ROW, so a pooled row survives across a repaint. Instrument the refusal REASON per press - pickup returns it and the screen surfaces it - and one run separates ERR_UNKNOWN_DROP from ERR_CLAIM_SPENT/ERR_UNKNOWN_REWARD. THE FIX HERE. Make any facade-level pickup path republish, so a state change a player can observe is visible wherever it was made. Do NOT satisfy this by adding view.refresh() to the failing test: that makes the suite green while the facade path stays invisible, which is the ADR 0066 quiet lie in a test. VERIFY BY: tools test --suite overflow green, then MUTATION-PROVE by removing the republish and confirming test_loot_overflow.gd:252-254 returns to red.

title: test_a_parked_drop_and_a_refused_drop_are_named_differently is red because the test bypasses the screen it then reads
source: read 2026-10-04 while mutation-proving the ERR_WORLD_FULL refusal label
next: THE RED. 'uv run python -m tools test --suite overflow' reports 45 passed / 1 failed on test_loot_overflow.gd:253, 'so the drop really is in the world: expected 1, got 0'. It is red WITH the ERR_WORLD_FULL fix in place, so it is pre-existing and NOT caused by that fix - I initially misread the mutation run as validating the fix and corrected that. THE CAUSE, read from source rather than inferred. _first_pickup (test_loot_overflow.gd:280-291) resolves the first claimable row and calls LootApi.pickup(actor, encounter_id, drop_id) DIRECTLY through the facade. That call mutates module state and returns; nothing tells the LootEncounterScreen to rebuild. The very next assertion (line 253) reads _rig.listed_reward(parked_view), and listed_reward (loot_screen_rig.gd:291-292) returns view.summary().get('reward', {}) - the screen's CACHED summary, taken before the pickup. So stashed_count reads 0 because the view never repainted, not because the drop was not parked. Lines 244-251 already PASSED, and those assert the facade return value is OK_OVERFLOW with ERR_INVENTORY_FULL, which proves _overflow DID park the drop and LootState is correct. The production path is fine; the observation is stale. THE REAL DEFECT THIS EXPOSES, and it is the one worth fixing. The panel does not repaint after a pickup driven by anything other than its own control. Criterion 2 WIRED OUT fails here in the shape that matters: a player presses Pick up, the bag does not grow, and the reward list still shows the drop as owed - the drop IS in the world, but the screen lies about it. That is the same stale-view family the boot probe reports as 'taking a drop left N of N pending; nothing was collected'. FIX OPTIONS, in preference order. (a) Make LootEncounterScreen subscribe to the loot state change and rebuild - the real fix, and it closes criterion 2 for this surface rather than for one test. (b) Have the test call view.refresh() after the facade call, which makes the test honest but leaves the player-facing lie in place - do NOT do this alone. (c) Assert against the facade's own post-state instead of the screen's cache, which tests LootState but stops testing the seam. ACCEPTANCE: after (a), this suite is green AND a real boot shows pending_drops falling and the bag row count growing after a row-control press. NOTE THE DOCSTRING BUG IN THE SAME FILE: _fill_inventory (line 317-322) says 'Spend every inventory slot, so every pickup has to overflow' but adds exactly ONE item. That is only correct because the rig is called with hero(1) - capacity 1 - so the single item fills it. The comment describes something the code does not do; fix the comment or the helper, because the next reader who passes hero() with the default capacity 24 gets a bag with 1 of 24 slots used and a pickup that succeeds instead of overflowing.

title: UNWIRED: the newborn is minted, returned and discarded - StatusLoop.tick writes result[born] and no production reader reads it
next: StatusLoop.tick (app/status_loop.gd:92) does result[born] = FertilityApi.advance(_actor, delta * SECONDS_PER_GESTATION_DAY) and returns the dictionary. item_workbench_app.gd:359 calls _status_loop.tick(delta) and DISCARDS the return value. Exhaustive grep of game/src for the key finds exactly one occurrence - the write at status_loop.gd:92. No reader in src/, no ui/, no screen. So the birth half of the pipeline terminates in a dictionary nobody opens: a child IS built, IS given a race through RaceApi.resolve_race, IS given per-lineage purity through BloodlineApi.inherit_from, and is then held only by PregnancyStatus.offspring (pregnancy.gd:29), which is ERASED at the end of the postpartum stage by FertilityApi.advance's actor.statuses.erase(status) (api.gd:162). The child therefore has a window of roughly ten seconds of game time (recovery_remaining = 10.0 / RECOVERY_RATE, api.gd:337) in which it exists, and no identity, no placement in a world, no roster entry and no save reference outside the mother's status. This is worse than the unwired producer above in one respect and better in another: better because the child IS constructed and IS correct, so the lineage maths is proven; worse because even if the gate opened tomorrow, the child would still be discarded. THE NEXT STEP IS NOT A TEST: it is a decision about what a newborn IS. Minimum viable: a caller that reads tick()['born'] and does something observable - add it to the settlement cast, register it in the roster, write it into the save payload. Note ADR 0089's rule that statuses are SESSION-only and never enter Actor.to_dict, so the child cannot ride the mother's save payload as a status - it needs a home of its own, which is a design question, not a wiring one. Also worth deciding at the same time: FertilityApi.roll_offspring_count (api.gd:174) has zero callers anywhere in game/src, so FertilityStats.MULTIPLE_BIRTH_CHANCE is contributed by the provider (provider.gd:22) and spent by nothing; resolve_offspring returns exactly one child unconditionally. Same shape: FertilityStats.PARTURITION_SAFETY and MATERNAL_RESILIENCE (provider.gd:20, :23) are contributed and read by nothing, so labor cannot fail and a birth cannot injure the mother.
